definition_zh: 狼；色狼；（狼吞虎咽地）吃
definition_en: a wild animal of the dog family that hunts in groups, or to eat food very quickly
core_image: 雪地上排成一线的灰色影子，低着头顺着气味往前赶
scene: 冬夜的雪地尽头，几点灰影成排地跟着气味移动，羊圈里的狗先叫了起来。A wolf circled the sheep pen twice before the dogs drove it off.
sceneCN: 这里 wolf 是「狼」（第 1 个义项：成群捕食的野生犬科动物）；句意为一只狼绕羊圈走了两圈，才被狗赶走。雪地上排成一线往前赶的灰影，就是这个词的印象。

collocations.phrase: keep the wolf from the door

derivatives.zh: 由 wolf 加形容词后缀 -ish 构成，义为「似狼的；贪婪的」
与 wolf 无直接词源关系的动物名，义为「狼獾；貂熊」

senses.title: The wild hunter
senses.definition: a wild animal of the dog family that lives and hunts in groups in forests and open country
senses.definitionCN: 在森林和旷野中成群生活的野生犬科动物
senses.example: A wolf circled the sheep pen twice before the dogs drove it off.
senses.exampleCN: 一只狼绕羊圈走了两圈，才被狗赶走。
senses.why: The word has named this animal since the oldest English records, so the animal is the whole meaning of the root.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从最早的英语文献起就指这种动物，所以动物的形象就是词根的全部意思。

senses.title: The predator of people
senses.definition: a man who hunts women in a cruel and unwanted way, used as a strong word of blame
senses.definitionCN: 以令人不快的方式纠缠女性的男人，用作强烈的贬斥
senses.example: The neighbours warned her about the wolf who hung around the bus stop.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们提醒她当心那个在公交站附近转悠的色狼。
senses.why: Because the animal is seen as a hunter of the helpless, the name slides onto a person who preys on others.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种动物被看作捕食无助者的猎手，这个名字就滑到了欺压他人的人身上。

senses.title: To eat like a hunter
senses.definition: to eat something very fast and in large bites, as a hungry animal would
senses.definitionCN: 像饿兽一样大口快速地吃
senses.example: He wolfed down two bowls of noodles before the train arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 火车到站前，他狼吞虎咽地吃下了两碗面。
senses.why: Turning the animal into a verb borrows its way of eating, so the name becomes an action.
senses.whyCN: 把动物名词变成动词，是借用了它吃东西的样子，于是名字变成了动作。

senses.title: The false alarm
senses.definition: to keep shouting about a danger that is not there, in the fixed phrase cry wolf
senses.definitionCN: 在没有危险时反复喊危险，用于固定说法 cry wolf
senses.example: If you cry wolf too often, nobody will believe you when it is real.
senses.exampleCN: 如果你总是谎报险情，真出事时便没人信你。
senses.why: The fable of the shepherd boy shows that the animal name can stand for empty warnings.
senses.whyCN: 牧童的寓言说明，这个动物名也可以代表空洞的警报。

intro.en: Wolf is an old Germanic animal name, shared with German Wolf and Dutch wolf, and traced back to a reconstructed root meaning the animal itself.
intro.cn: wolf 是古老的日耳曼语动物名，与德语 Wolf、荷兰语 wolf 同源，可上溯到一个重构词根，意思就是这种动物。

items.en: wulf was the ordinary name of the animal in Old English poetry and law.
items.cn: wulf 是古英语诗歌与法律中这种动物的常称。

items.en: The same name appears across the Germanic languages, which shows how old it is.
items.cn: 同一个名字出现在各门日耳曼语里，可见其古老。

items.en: Norse settlers brought forms such as ulfr, which mixed with the English word.
items.cn: 北欧移民带来 ulfr 这样的形式，与英语词混在一起。

items.en: The plural wolves settled in, keeping the old change of f to v between vowels.
items.cn: 复数 wolves 固定下来，保留了元音之间 f 变 v 的古老规则。

items.en: The animal sense stayed, and the verb to wolf down grew out of its greedy eating.
items.cn: 动物义保留至今，动词 wolf down 则由它贪婪的吃相长出来。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same animal stem, the second holds other wild hunters and their kin.
note.cn: 第一组收同根而生的词，第二组收其他野生猎手及其同类。

entries.definition: More than one wolf.
Looking or behaving like a wolf.
Eats something very quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 狼吞虎咽（第三人称单数）

entries.definition: A small wild animal of the dog family with a pointed face.
A wild animal like a small wolf that often feeds on dead animals.
A wild animal of North America, like a small wolf.

normalIntro.en: Wolf is short and old: three consonants frame one round vowel, and only the plural changes its shape.
normalIntro.cn: wolf 又短又古老：三个辅音夹着一个圆元音，只有复数会变形。

normal.en: The w at the front and the lf at the back hold the vowel like jaws.
normal.cn: 前面的 w 和后面的 lf 像上下颌一样夹住元音。

normal.en: Plural wolves keeps the old habit of turning f into v between vowels.
normal.cn: 复数 wolves 保留了元音之间 f 变 v 的老习惯。

normal.en: Wolf down means to eat as fast as a hungry wolf.
normal.cn: wolf down 就是像饿狼一样吃得飞快。

normal.en: Cry wolf comes from the fable of the shepherd boy.
normal.cn: cry wolf 来自牧童的寓言。

normal.en: A lone wolf is a person who keeps away from the group, just like the animal that hunts alone.
normal.cn: lone wolf 指离群的人，正如独自捕猎的狼。

abstract.en: Grey shapes moving in a line through snow.
abstract.cn: 雪地上一排灰影顺着一条线移动。

abstract.en: A ring of eyes at the edge of the firelight.
abstract.cn: 火光边缘围成一圈的眼睛。

abstract.en: Hunger made visible as a body that never stands still.
abstract.cn: 饥饿变成了一个永不停下的身体。

examples.en: A wolf howled somewhere behind the hill and the whole village fell silent.
examples.cn: 山后某处传来一声狼嚎，整个村子静了下来。

examples.en: Do not cry wolf unless you really see the danger.
examples.cn: 除非真的看到危险，否则不要谎报险情。

examples.en: The boy wolfed down his breakfast and ran for the school bus.
examples.cn: 男孩狼吞虎咽地吃完早饭，跑着去赶校车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呜尔夫」——夜里一声长长的「呜」，就是狼在叫。

root: 古英语 wulf（狼），源自日耳曼语共同词形，与德语 Wolf 同源；复数 wolves 保留了 f 在元音间变 v 的古规则。

sensesIntro.en: The animal comes first, then the person who preys on others, then the act of eating like the animal, then the empty alarm.
sensesIntro.cn: 先有动物，再有像动物一样欺压别人的人，接着是像动物一样吃，最后是空洞的警报。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey hunter moving in a line through snow.
core.cn: 核心意象：雪地上一线前行的灰色猎手。

branches.en: The animal branch: a wolf circling the sheep pen.
branches.cn: 动物分支：绕着羊圈转的狼。

branches.en: The human branch: the name turned into an insult.
branches.cn: 人分支：名字变成了骂词。

branches.en: The eating branch: the animal name becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 吃分支：动物名变成动词。

branches.en: The alarm branch: the animal stands for a false warning.
branches.cn: 警报分支：动物代表虚假的警告。

branches.en: The character branch: the way a creature eats becomes a way a person eats.
branches.cn: 品性分支：动物的吃法成了人的吃法。

intro.en: Wolf is a single native stem with no living prefix or suffix; the plural ending is the only inflection it carries.
intro.cn: wolf 是一个单独的本土词干，不带活的词缀；它唯一的屈折变化是复数词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, so no Latin ancestor exists; the Latin words below are distant cousins from the same old family.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词只是同属古老语系的远亲。

items.meaning: a wild animal of the dog family
items.example: The stem carries the whole meaning.
It appears in wolfish and werewolf.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 wolfish 与 werewolf 里。

items.example: It forms wolfish, like a wolf.

items.meaning: a man who becomes a wolf
items.example: The old word for man joins the stem.
items.exampleCN: 「人」的古词与这个词干合在一起。

items.meaning: a large dog bred to hunt wolves
items.example: Hound is the old word for dog.
The animal name colours the sound.
items.exampleCN: 动物名为这个声音染上色彩。

definition_zh: 妇女；成年女子；女人（统称）
definition_en: an adult female human being
core_image: 菜市场里拎着两袋菜还能一只手接电话的成年女性身影
scene: 早市的过道上，一位提着两袋菜的中年人边走边和邻居商量孩子上学的事。A woman stopped to help the old man pick up the coins he had dropped.
sceneCN: 这里 woman 是「成年女子」（第 1 个义项：成年的女性人类）；句意为一位女士停下来帮老人捡起掉落的硬币。市场里拎着菜还能一手接电话的成年女性身影，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 woman 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「有女性气质的；端庄的」
由 woman 加 -hood 构成，义为「女性身份；妇女成年期」
由动词 womanize 加 -er 构成，义为「玩弄女性的人」

senses.title: An adult female person
senses.definition: a fully grown female human being, seen as an individual
senses.definitionCN: 成年的女性人类，作为一个个体来看
senses.example: A woman stopped to help the old man pick up the coins he had dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 一位女士停下来帮老人捡起掉落的硬币。
senses.why: This is the plainest use: the word points at one grown-up female person.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的用法：这个词直接指向一位成年的女性。

senses.title: The female side of us all
senses.definition: the female members of a group or of people in general, taken together
senses.definitionCN: 某个群体或整个人类中的女性成员，合在一起说
senses.example: The hall was full of women waiting for the hiring results.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里坐满了等待招聘结果的女人。
senses.why: Stressing the first part makes the word work as a general label rather than as a description of one person.
senses.whyCN: 把重音放在前面，这个词就成了一个统称，而不是描述某一个人。

senses.title: The old servant sense
senses.definition: in older English, a female servant or the housekeeper of a household
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的英语中，指女仆或家中管事的女仆
senses.example: In the old household books, the woman was paid each quarter for the washing.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的家用账本里，那位女仆每季度领取洗衣的工钱。
senses.why: Because servants were so often women, the bare word could stand for the office itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为仆人多为女性，这个不加修饰的词可以代指那个职务。

intro.en: Woman is Old English wifmann, a compound of wif, meaning female, and mann, meaning person; only later did mann narrow to the male.
intro.cn: woman 来自古英语 wifmann，由 wif（女性）与 mann（人）复合而成；man 后来才缩小为指男性。

items.en: wifmann joined wif, a female, with mann, a human being.
items.cn: wifmann 把表示女性的 wif 与表示人的 mann 结合。

items.en: Like other compounds, it kept the plural wifmenn, with the same vowel change.
items.cn: 与其他复合词一样，它保留了复数 wifmenn，并有同样的元音变化。

items.en: The two parts blended and the first became wo-, giving womman.
items.cn: 两部分融在一起，前一部分变成 wo-，写作 womman。

items.en: The spelling settled as woman with the plural women, keeping the old rounded vowel.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 woman，复数为 women，保留了古老的圆元音。

items.en: Once man came to mean an adult male, the compound was heard as one word, not a phrase.
items.cn: 当 man 转而指成年男性之后，这个复合词就只被当作一个词听，而不是一个短语。

note.en: The first group holds the plural and the words built on the same stem, the second holds other words for a female person.
note.cn: 第一组收复数与同根词，第二组收其他指女性的词。

entries.definition: More than one woman.
Having the qualities thought typical of a woman.
The state of being an adult woman.
A polite word for a woman, now often a little formal.
Of the sex that gives birth, or a person of that sex.
A female child or young person.

normalIntro.en: Woman is an old compound that has worn smooth: wif once meant female and mann once meant person.
normalIntro.cn: woman 是一个被磨旧的古老复合词：wif 原指女性，mann 原指人。

normal.en: The plural women is not spelled with a second o, only the sound changes.
normal.cn: 复数 women 不写第二个 o，变的只是发音。

normal.en: The first part once meant female, so woman says female person from the inside.
normal.cn: 前半部分原意是女性，所以 woman 从字的内部说「女性的人」。

normal.en: Man did not mean adult male at first, which is why woman is not a shortened form of it.
normal.cn: man 最初并不指成年男性，所以 woman 并不是它缩短来的。

normal.en: Womanly adds the adjective ending; womanhood adds the ending for a state.
normal.cn: womanly 加形容词词尾；womanhood 加表示状态的词尾。

normal.en: A woman of her word keeps promises, a phrase that plays on the word word.
normal.cn: a woman of her word 指守信的女人，是拿 word 做的双关。

abstract.en: Two hands holding rice bags and a phone at the same time.
abstract.cn: 两只手同时拎着米袋和手机。

abstract.en: A shoulder turned to carry a child who has fallen asleep.
abstract.cn: 肩膀侧过来，让睡着的孩子靠上。

abstract.en: A voice that ends an argument without raising itself.
abstract.cn: 一个不用提高音量就结束争论的声音。

examples.en: The woman at the desk asked for my name twice.
examples.cn: 柜台后那位女士把我的名字问了两次。

examples.en: More women than men applied for the job this year.
examples.cn: 今年申请这份工作的女性比男性多。

examples.en: She is a woman of her word and always brings the books back on time.
examples.cn: 她说话算话，总是按时把书还回来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝闷」——家里忙得窝闷闷转的，多是成年女子。

root: 古英语 wifmann 复合词：wif（女性）+ mann（人），复数 wifmenn；后来 mann 缩小词义，woman 遂成为女性的独立称谓。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as one grown-up female person, widens into women as a group, and narrows in old texts to the female servant.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一位成年女性出发，扩展为作为整体的女性，又在旧文本中收窄为女仆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grown woman carrying bags and a phone at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：同时拎着菜和手机的成年女性。

branches.en: The individual branch: a woman helping an old man.
branches.cn: 个体分支：扶起老人的女士。

branches.en: The group branch: a hall full of waiting women.
branches.cn: 群体分支：满厅等待的女性。

branches.en: The servant branch: the woman paid for the washing.
branches.cn: 仆人分支：领洗衣工钱的女仆。

branches.en: The language branch: woman appears in titles and in fixed polite phrases.
branches.cn: 语言分支：woman 见于头衔与固定客套语。

branches.en: The role branch: a general word that once named a job.
branches.cn: 角色分支：一个统称词曾用作职务名。

intro.en: Woman was once two native words joined, and the second half still carries the old sense of person.
intro.cn: woman 原是两个本土词拼在一起，后半部分至今还带着「人」的旧义。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below belong to a different old branch.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词属另一支古老的语系。

items.example: The compound has become one word.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词已经融为一体。

items.example: It gives women through an old vowel change.
items.exampleCN: 它通过古老的元音变化得 women。

items.meaning: to make or act in a way
items.meaningCN: 使成为或以某种方式行事

items.example: Its Old English form headed the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它的古英语形式曾是这个复合词的第一部分。

items.meaning: once a person, now an adult male
items.example: The narrowing of this word shaped woman.
items.exampleCN: 这个词义的缩小塑造了 woman。

definition_zh: 想知道；纳闷；感到惊讶；惊奇；奇迹；奇观
definition_en: to want to know something, or to feel surprise and admiration; also the feeling or the thing that causes it
core_image: 夜里抬头看见满天星，脖子一直往后仰，忘了低头
scene: 孩子第一次被带到郊外，抬头看星星看了很久，一句话也不说。I wonder whether the old shop is still open after all these years.
sceneCN: 这里 wonder 是「想知道」（第 1 个义项：心里存着疑问，很想知道答案）；句意为我想知道这么多年过去那家老店是否还开着。夜里仰头看满天星，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 奇迹；奇观；令人惊叹的事物

derivatives.zh: 由 wonder 加 -ful 构成，义为「极好的；精彩的」
由 wonder 加 -ing 构成，义为「好奇的；疑惑的」
由 wonder 加 -ous 构成，义为「奇妙的；令人惊叹的」
由 wonder 加 -ment 构成，义为「惊奇；惊讶之情」

senses.title: To want to know
senses.definition: to feel a wish to know something, often said softly before a polite question
senses.definitionCN: 心里很想弄明白某事，常用在礼貌的提问之前
senses.example: I wonder whether the old shop is still open after all these years.
senses.exampleCN: 我想知道这么多年过去那家老店是否还开着。
senses.why: The old root means to gaze in astonishment, and a mind that keeps gazing turns into a mind that keeps asking.
senses.whyCN: 古老的词根意思是惊讶地凝视，一直望下去的心就变成了不断发问的心。

senses.title: To be struck by something
senses.definition: to feel surprise mixed with admiration when something is greater than expected
senses.definitionCN: 遇到超出预期的事物时，感到惊讶又钦佩
senses.example: The children wondered at the size of the whale in the museum hall.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们望着大厅里那头鲸的骨架，惊讶得说不出话。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the body stops and stares because the sight is too large to take in.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：身体停下凝视，因为眼前的景象大得接不住。

senses.title: The feeling itself
senses.definition: the feeling of surprise and admiration that such a sight leaves behind
senses.definitionCN: 那样的景象留下的那份惊讶与钦佩
senses.example: She looked at the night sky with wonder, forgetting the cold.
senses.exampleCN: 她满怀惊奇地望着夜空，忘了冷。
senses.why: Once the staring ends, what remains inside is the feeling, so the name turns into a noun.
senses.whyCN: 凝视结束之后，留在心里的是那种感受，于是这个名字变成了名词。

senses.title: The thing that causes it
senses.definition: a person or thing so extraordinary that it makes people stare and admire
senses.definitionCN: 极其非凡、让人驻足赞叹的人或物
senses.example: The bridge was counted among the wonders of the ancient world.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥被列为古代世界的奇观之一。
senses.why: By a natural shift, the cause of the staring takes the same name as the staring itself.
senses.whyCN: 很自然的一次转移，让引起凝视的东西和凝视本身用了同一个名字。

intro.en: Wonder comes from Old English wundor, a noun for a marvel, related to words for astonishment in the other Germanic languages.
intro.cn: wonder 来自古英语名词 wundor（奇事），与其他日耳曼语中表示惊讶的词同源。

items.en: wundor named a marvel or a portent, something that stopped people in their tracks.
items.cn: wundor 指奇事或征兆，是让人停下脚步的东西。

items.en: Cousin words in the old Germanic languages also mean a marvel, which points to one shared root.
items.cn: 各门古老日耳曼语里的同源词也表示奇事，指向一个共同词根。

items.en: The noun softened to wonder and gained the sense of a feeling as well as a thing.
items.cn: 名词演变为 wonder，既指事物，也开始指一种感受。

items.en: The verb to wonder developed, first meaning to marvel at, then to be curious.
items.cn: 动词兴起来，先表示对某事惊叹，后来表示好奇。

items.en: The polite opener of requests, as in wonder if, became fixed in everyday speech.
items.cn: 作为礼貌开场的 wonder if，在日常口语中固定下来。

note.en: The first group holds the same stem in other shapes, the second holds other words for curiosity and surprise.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干的其他形态，第二组收其他表示好奇与惊讶的词。

entries.definition: Extremely good or enjoyable.
Feeling curious or puzzled.
Marvellous, amazing, a little literary.
To be filled with wonder, or a wonderful thing.
A strong wish to know or learn something.
A feeling of respect mixed with wonder and fear.

normalIntro.en: Wonder is one stem used as verb and noun: the same word means to stare, to ask, and the thing worth staring at.
normalIntro.cn: wonder 是同一个词干兼作动词和名词：既指凝视，也指发问，还指值得凝视的东西。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling, so context alone tells you which is meant.
normal.cn: 名词和动词拼写相同，只能靠上下文判断。

normal.en: No wonder is a frozen phrase that still carries the old idea of marvel.
normal.cn: no wonder 是固定说法，仍带着「奇事」的旧意。

normal.en: Add -ful and the marvel becomes an adjective of praise: wonderful.
normal.cn: 加 -ful，奇事就变成赞美的形容词 wonderful。

normal.en: Wonder if is the soft way to ask a question, not a claim of not knowing.
normal.cn: wonder if 是婉转发问的方式，不是在声称不知道。

normal.en: Wonder and wander differ by one letter: one stays still and stares, the other walks away.
normal.cn: wonder 与 wander 只差一个字母：一个驻足凝视，一个走开。

abstract.en: A neck tipped back so far that the sky fills the whole face.
abstract.cn: 脖子仰得太久，整张脸都是天空。

abstract.en: A question that has no sharp edges yet.
abstract.cn: 一个还没有长出尖角的问题。

abstract.en: A hand lifted but not yet touching the stone of the old bridge.
abstract.cn: 手举起来了，却还没碰到老桥的石头。

examples.en: I wonder why she left without saying goodbye.
examples.cn: 我想知道她为什么不告而别。

examples.en: The children stared at the sea in wonder.
examples.cn: 孩子们惊奇地望着大海。

examples.en: It is no wonder that he passed the exam after months of study.
examples.cn: 他苦读了几个月，通过考试一点也不奇怪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「望的」——一直往前望着的那个东西，就是让人惊奇的「奇迹」。

root: 古英语名词 wundor（奇事、奇迹），与日耳曼语同源词共同指向「惊奇地凝视」这一核心意象；后派生动词义。

sensesIntro.en: From a stopped body the meaning spreads: first to be struck, then to be curious, then to the feeling, and finally to the thing worth staring at.
sensesIntro.cn: 意义从一个停住的身体散开：先是感到震撼，再是好奇，接着是那份感受，最后是值得凝视的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a neck tipped back until the sky fills the face.
core.cn: 核心意象：仰头到整张脸都是天空。

branches.en: The asking branch: a soft question about the old shop.
branches.cn: 发问分支：轻声问起那家老店。

branches.en: The staring branch: children lost before a whale skeleton.
branches.cn: 凝视分支：孩子在鲸骨架前出神。

branches.en: The feeling branch: wonder under the night sky.
branches.cn: 感受分支：夜空下的惊奇。

branches.en: The marvel branch: a bridge counted among ancient wonders.
branches.cn: 奇观分支：跻身古代奇迹的桥。

branches.en: The everyday branch: no wonder marks surprise that has become ordinary.
branches.cn: 日常分支：no wonder 标记已经平常的惊讶。

intro.en: Wonder is a plain Germanic stem; the endings it takes, such as -ful and -ous, only colour the marvel into adjectives.
intro.cn: wonder 是朴素的日耳曼语词干；它加上的 -ful、-ous 等词尾，只把这件奇事染成形容词。

latinIntro.en: The stem is native Germanic, so there is no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below are cousins of the same idea only.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词只是同一想法的表亲。

items.meaning: a marvel, or to stare and ask
items.example: The stem carries both noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干兼作名词与动词。

items.example: The old marvel sense survives here.
items.exampleCN: 古老的奇事义在此保留。

items.example: The participle shows the stopped body.
items.exampleCN: 分词部分呈现停住的身体。

definition_zh: 极好的；精彩的；美妙的；令人惊叹的
definition_en: extremely good, pleasant, or impressive, so that it makes you stop and admire
core_image: 端上一盘刚出锅的菜，全桌人同时「哇」了一声
scene: 第一次尝到朋友做的家乡菜，桌上几个人都放下筷子先看着它。The view from the top of the pass was wonderful in the early morning light.
sceneCN: 这里 wonderful 是「极好的、美妙的」（第 1 个义项：好到让人惊叹）；句意为清晨光线下从山口望下去的景致美得惊人。一桌人同时「哇」出声，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wonderful 加 -ly 构成，义为「极好地；奇妙地」
由 wonderful 加 -ness 构成，义为「美妙；极好」
去掉 -ful 得到的名词，义为「惊奇；奇迹」

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: so good or pleasant that it draws praise without effort
senses.definitionCN: 好得或愉快得让人自然而然地称赞
senses.example: We had a wonderful time at the small restaurant by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在河边那家小馆子度过了非常愉快的时光。
senses.why: The suffix -ful says full of, so the marvel of wonder is poured into a whole adjective of praise.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ful 表示「充满」，于是 wonder 的惊奇被灌进一个纯粹赞美的形容词。

senses.title: Marvellous to look at
senses.definition: so striking or beautiful that people stop to admire it
senses.definitionCN: 非常醒目的、美的，让人停下来欣赏
senses.example: The view from the top of the pass was wonderful in the early morning light.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨光线下，从山口望下去的景致美得惊人。
senses.why: The older layer of wonder means a marvel, and the landscape here still keeps that sense of staring.
senses.whyCN: wonder 更古老的一层意思是奇事，这里的风景仍保留着那种凝视的感觉。

senses.title: Remarkably skilled or kind
senses.definition: used of a person or a quality that is better than one expects
senses.definitionCN: 用于人或某种品质，好得超出预期
senses.example: Her wonderful patience made the long wait almost pleasant.
senses.exampleCN: 她那了不起的耐心让漫长的等待几乎变得愉快。
senses.why: Praise moves from things to people, so the same adjective describes a quality that impresses.
senses.whyCN: 称赞从物转到人，同一个形容词便用来描述令人佩服的品质。

intro.en: Wonderful is the native noun wonder, a marvel, with the suffix -ful added to say full of marvels.
intro.cn: wonderful 由本土名词 wonder（奇事）加后缀 -ful 构成，意为「充满奇事的」。

items.en: The noun wundor named a marvel, and the suffix -ful meant full of.
items.cn: 名词 wundor 指奇事，后缀 -ful 表示充满。

items.en: The two parts joined as wonderful in the sense of full of wonders.
items.cn: 两部分组合成 wonderful，意思满是奇事。

items.en: Everyday speech stretched it into a general word of praise.
items.cn: 日常口语把它引申为泛用的赞美词。

items.en: The gradable use with more and most settled, since the suffix blocks -er.
items.cn: 因为后缀不能用 -er，比较级与最高级固定用 more 和 most。

items.en: In current use the adjective is milder than the noun, closer to very good than to miraculous.
items.cn: 如今这个形容词比名词温和，更接近「很好」而不是「奇迹般」。

note.en: The first group holds words cut from the same stem, the second holds other adjectives of strong praise.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干切出的词，第二组收其他表示强烈赞美的形容词。

entries.definition: A marvel, or the feeling of amazement.
In an excellent or marvellous way.
Marvellous, chiefly literary.
Extremely good or surprising, British spelling.
Extremely good, informal and enthusiastic.
Impressive and fine, a little formal.

normalIntro.en: Wonderful is wonder plus the ending -ful, so the word literally says full of marvels.
normalIntro.cn: wonderful 就是 wonder 加 -ful，字面上就是「满是奇事」。

normal.en: Keep the double l of -ful: only the adverb wonderfully adds one more l before -y.
normal.cn: 记住 -ful 里的双 l：只有副词 wonderfully 会在 -y 前再多一个 l。

normal.en: The ending -ful means full of, so wonderful is full of wonder.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ful 表示充满，所以 wonderful 就是满是惊奇。

normal.en: Because of the suffix, the comparison takes more and most, never -er.
normal.cn: 由于这个后缀，比较级用 more 和 most，从不用 -er。

normal.en: Wonderfully adds -ly and keeps both l letters, giving three in a row.
normal.cn: wonderfully 加 -ly 时保留两个 l，于是连出三个 l。

normal.en: Wonder is the noun and wonderful the adjective, a pair like help and helpful.
normal.cn: wonder 是名词，wonderful 是形容词，正像 help 与 helpful 这一对。

abstract.en: A whole table going quiet at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 整桌人在同一瞬间安静下来。

abstract.en: Light on water that makes the eye refuse to blink.
abstract.cn: 水上的光让眼睛不愿意眨。

abstract.en: A word that has grown lighter than its root.
abstract.cn: 一个比它的词根更轻的词。

examples.en: Thank you for a wonderful evening.
examples.cn: 谢谢你给了我这么一个愉快的夜晚。

examples.en: It was a wonderful surprise to see her at the station.
examples.cn: 在车站见到她真是个美妙的惊喜。

examples.en: The old gardener told wonderful stories about the trees.
examples.cn: 老园丁讲了很多关于这些树的奇妙故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「万得福」——万事都得到福气，日子当然「极好」。

root: 古英语 wundor（奇事）+ 本土后缀 -ful（充满）→ wonderful；词根意象是「惊奇地凝视」。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from things that are simply very good, to sights that stop people, and finally to people who impress.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从单纯很好的事物，走到让人停步的景象，最后走到令人佩服的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole table going quiet at the first taste.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一口之后整桌人安静下来。

branches.en: The praise branch: a wonderful evening at a small restaurant.
branches.cn: 赞美分支：小馆子里的愉快夜晚。

branches.en: The sight branch: a pass lit by early sun.
branches.cn: 景象分支：晨光里的山口。

branches.en: The person branch: patience that impresses everyone.
branches.cn: 人分支：让人佩服的耐心。

branches.en: The mild branch: current use is gentler than the noun.
branches.cn: 温和分支：今用比名词温和。

branches.en: The gradable branch: more wonderful, most wonderful.
branches.cn: 程度分支：more wonderful、most wonderful。

intro.en: Wonderful is a native stem plus the old suffix -ful, and it is that suffix which shapes the comparison.
intro.cn: wonderful 是本土词干加古老后缀 -ful，正是这个后缀决定了它的比较级写法。

latinIntro.en: Neither part is Latin; the words below are borrowed cousins of the same idea of marvel.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不是拉丁语；下面的词只是借来的、同表「奇迹」这一想法的表亲。

items.exampleCN: 它由 wonder 构成 wonderful。

items.example: It is replaced by more wonderful.
The same stem forms this noun.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干可构成这个名词。
它构成文学色彩的 wondrous。

definition_zh: 木材；木头；树林；林地；木（球杆；乐器类别）
definition_en: the hard material of trees used for building, or a small forest; also the hard core of a golf club
core_image: 刚锯开的木头横截面，年轮一圈套一圈，还带着潮气
scene: 院子里新锯断的树桩还没搬走，切面上能数出一圈圈的年轮。The table is made of old oak wood that has turned dark with time.
sceneCN: 这里 wood 是「木材、木头」（第 1 个义项：树木的坚硬材料，用来做东西）；句意为这张桌子是用年久变深的老橡木做的。新锯开的横截面上能数出年轮，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wood 加 -en 构成，义为「木制的；僵硬的」
由 wood 加 -y 构成，义为「木质化的；树木茂密的」
由 wood 与 land 复合，义为「林地」
由 wood 与 work 复合，义为「木工活；木制部件」

senses.title: The material of a tree
senses.definition: the hard substance inside a tree, cut and used for building or burning
senses.definitionCN: 树干内部的坚硬物质，砍下后用于建造或燃烧
senses.example: The table is made of old oak wood that has turned dark with time.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子是用年久变深的老橡木做的。
senses.why: The oldest meaning is the substance itself, the part of the tree that can be carried away and used.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是那种物质本身，也就是树身上能够搬走使用的那部分。

senses.title: A small forest
senses.definition: a piece of land covered with growing trees, smaller than a forest, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 一片长着活树的土地，比 forest 小，常用复数
senses.example: We walked through the woods behind the farm until it got dark.
senses.exampleCN: 我们穿过农舍后面的树林，一直走到天黑。
senses.why: Where the material grows in plenty, the same name serves for the place, and the plural marks the many trees.
senses.whyCN: 那种材料长得多的地方也用了同一个名字，复数则点出许多棵树。

senses.title: The hard core of a club
senses.definition: the solid block of a golf club that strikes the ball, once made of wood
senses.definitionCN: 高尔夫球杆击球的那块实心部分，早年用木头制成
senses.example: He hit the ball with the wood instead of the iron on the short hole.
senses.exampleCN: 那洞很短，他用木杆而不是铁杆击球。
senses.why: Because clubs were once carved from hard timber, the material name stuck to the part.
senses.whyCN: 因为球杆早年用硬木削成，材料名就留在了那个部件上。

senses.title: A wooden sound
senses.definition: used to describe a wooden or dull quality, or the section of an orchestra that was once wooden
senses.definitionCN: 用来形容木质的、发闷的特质，也指乐团中过去用木制成的声部
senses.example: The wood section began softly, and the strings came in a beat later.
senses.exampleCN: 木管声部轻轻开始，弦乐晚了一拍进来。
senses.why: Material used as an adjective easily becomes a label for sound or class, not only for substance.
senses.whyCN: 材料名作形容词用，很容易变成声音或类别的标签，而不只是指物质。

intro.en: Wood is Old English wudu, meaning both the tree and its timber, and the same stem survives in the Dutch and German names for wood.
intro.cn: wood 来自古英语 wudu，既指树也指木材，同一词干还见于荷兰语和德语的「木头」。

items.en: wudu named both a growing tree and the timber cut from it.
items.cn: wudu 既指生长着的树，也指砍下的木材。

items.en: Cousin words in Dutch and German still mean wood or forest.
items.cn: 荷兰语与德语的同源词仍表示木头或森林。

items.en: The final vowel weakened, and the form settled toward wode and later wood.
items.cn: 词尾元音弱化，形式向 wode 过渡，最终成为 wood。

items.en: The wooden adjective took the old ending -en, as in golden and silken.
items.cn: 木制的形容词采用了古老的词尾 -en，就像 golden 与 silken。

items.en: The plural woods narrowed mostly to the place sense, the trees standing together.
items.cn: 复数 woods 主要收窄到地方义，即聚在一起的树。

note.en: The first group holds words grown from the same stem, the second holds other words for timber and for small forests.
note.cn: 第一组收同根长出的词，第二组收其他泛指木材与树林的词。

entries.definition: Made of wood; also stiff and unnatural.
Having a lot of wood in it, or full of trees.
Land covered with trees.
Wood prepared for building, often large beams.
Timber cut into rough boards, chiefly American.
A large area thickly covered with trees.

normalIntro.en: Wood is one short native word with a double life: growing trees and the timber cut from them.
normalIntro.cn: wood 是一个简短的本土词，过着双重生活：既指活树，也指砍下来的木头。

normal.en: The plural woods usually means a place full of trees, not several materials.
normal.cn: 复数 woods 通常指满是树的地方，而不是好几种木头。

normal.en: Wooden takes the old ending -en, the same one in golden.
normal.cn: wooden 用古老的词尾 -en，与 golden 相同。

normal.en: Woody adds -y and keeps both letters of the stem: wood plus y.
normal.cn: woody 加 -y 时保留词干的两个字母：wood 加 y。

normal.en: Do not confuse wood with would: one is material, the other a helping verb.
normal.cn: 别把 wood 与 would 混了：一个是材料，一个是助动词。

normal.en: Woodland and woodwork are compounds that join a second common word.
normal.cn: woodland 与 woodwork 都是复合词，后面接一个常用词。

abstract.en: Rings counted on a fresh stump.
abstract.cn: 在新鲜的树桩上数年轮。

abstract.en: A grain that pulls a nail slightly to one side.
abstract.cn: 木纹让钉子微微歪向一边。

abstract.en: Warmth that comes from a wall of old beams.
abstract.cn: 一面旧梁柱墙传来的温度。

examples.en: The old chair is carved from a single block of wood.
examples.cn: 这把旧椅子是用一整块木头雕成的。

examples.en: They gathered dry wood for the fire before nightfall.
examples.cn: 天黑前他们捡好了烧火用的干柴。

examples.en: A path runs through the woods behind the village school.
examples.cn: 一条小路穿过村小学后面的林子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「屋的」——盖屋子用的，正是木材。

root: 古英语 wudu（树；木材），与荷兰语、德语同源；加 -en 得 wooden，加 -y 得 woody。

sensesIntro.en: The material comes first, then the place where it grows, then the part of an object once cut from it, and finally the dull wooden quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是材料，再是长材料的地方，接着是用它削成的部件，最后是发闷的木质质感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rings counted on a freshly cut stump.
core.cn: 核心意象：在刚锯开的树桩上数年轮。

branches.en: The material branch: a table of old oak wood.
branches.cn: 材料分支：老橡木做的桌子。

branches.en: The place branch: a walk through the woods at dusk.
branches.cn: 地方分支：黄昏穿过林子。

branches.en: The club branch: a wooden head striking the ball.
branches.cn: 球杆分支：木制杆头击球。

branches.en: The sound branch: the wood section of an orchestra.
branches.cn: 声音分支：乐团的木管声部。

branches.en: The quality branch: wood as a word for stiffness and dullness.
branches.cn: 质感分支：wood 用来形容僵硬与发闷。

intro.en: Wood is a bare native stem; the endings -en and -y are what turn the material into adjectives.
intro.cn: wood 是一个不带词缀的本土词干；把材料变成形容词的是 -en 与 -y 两个词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic with no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below name the same material from another branch.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词从另一支语系来指同一种材料。

items.meaning: tree material or a small forest

items.exampleCN: 它使 wood 成为 woods。

items.meaning: a task or a made thing
a picture printed from a wood block

definition_zh: 木制的；木头的；僵硬的；呆板的；生硬的
definition_en: made of wood, or stiff and unnatural in movement or manner
core_image: 一只雕得正好的木手，纹路对，可是弯不下去
scene: 旧教堂里那排椅子全是硬木做的，坐上去一动就会响。The actor gave a wooden performance that made the whole audience sit still.
sceneCN: 这里 wooden 是「木制的」（第 1 个义项：用木头做成的）；句意是那个演员演得呆板僵硬，让全场观众都坐得直直的。雕得正好却弯不下去的木手，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wooden 加 -ly 构成，义为「呆板地；僵硬地」
由 wooden 加 -ness 构成，义为「呆板；僵硬」
去掉 -en 得到的名词，义为「木材；树林」

senses.title: Made of timber
senses.definition: made from the hard material of a tree, especially for furniture or tools
senses.definitionCN: 用树木的坚硬材料制成，尤指家具或工具
senses.example: The long rows of seats in the old church were wooden and squeaked.
senses.exampleCN: 老教堂里那排长长的座椅都是木制的，一坐就吱呀响。
senses.why: The old ending -en means made of, so the material name becomes an adjective of substance.
senses.whyCN: 古老的词尾 -en 表示「由……制成」，于是材料名变成了表示材质的形容词。

senses.title: Stiff like dead timber
senses.definition: moving or bending awkwardly, as if the body had no joints
senses.definitionCN: 动作笨拙生硬，像身体没有关节一样
senses.example: His wooden movements at the dance made everyone smile.
senses.exampleCN: 他在舞会上僵硬的舞步让大家都会心一笑。
senses.why: Wood does not bend, so a person who moves like a board is described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 木头不会弯，因此动作像木板的人就用同一个词来形容。

senses.title: Unnatural in manner
senses.definition: stiff and without warmth in voice, expression or performance
senses.definitionCN: 声音、表情或表演僵硬而没有温度
senses.example: The actor gave a wooden performance that made the whole audience sit still.
senses.exampleCN: 那个演员演得呆板僵硬，让全场观众都坐得直直的。
senses.why: From bodies the meaning spreads to manner: a face or a voice that shows no living change is wooden too.
senses.whyCN: 从身体延伸到举止：一张不会变化的脸、一个不起伏的声音同样是 wooden。

intro.en: Wooden is the Old English noun wudu with the old adjective ending -en, which says made of.
intro.cn: wooden 是古英语名词 wudu 加上古老的形容词词尾 -en，意思是「由……制成」。

items.en: wudu was the material, and the ending -en marked a thing made of it.
items.cn: wudu 是那种材料，词尾 -en 标注由它制成的东西。

items.en: The same ending built golden and silken, which is why the forms look alike.
items.cn: 同一个词尾也造出 golden 与 silken，所以这些形式看起来很相似。

items.en: The form settled as wooden, and the unstressed ending lost its vowel sound.
items.cn: 形式固定为 wooden，非重读的词尾失去了元音的音值。

items.en: The literal sense held, and the figurative sense of stiff followed naturally.
items.cn: 字面义保留，僵硬这一比喻义随之自然出现。

items.en: Today the adjective describes acting and speech as often as furniture.
items.cn: 今天这个形容词形容表演和说话，几乎和形容家具一样频繁。

note.en: The first group holds other words ending in the old made-of suffix, the second holds adjectives of stiffness.
note.cn: 第一组收其他带「由……制成」这个词尾的词，第二组收表示僵硬的形容词。

entries.definition: The material of trees.
Full of wood or trees.
Made of gold, or gold in colour.
Hard to bend, or not relaxed.
Fixed and unable to bend.
Showing no energy or feeling.

normalIntro.en: Wooden is wood plus the old -en that means made of, the same ending as in golden.
normalIntro.cn: wooden 是 wood 加表示「由……制成」的古老 -en，与 golden 的词尾相同。

normal.en: Wood plus en gives wooden, with no extra letter dropped.
normal.cn: wood 加 en 就是 wooden，中间不落字母。

normal.en: The ending -en means made of, as in golden and silken.
normal.cn: -en 表示「由……制成」，如 golden 与 silken。

normal.en: Because it already ends in -en, the comparison uses more wooden.
normal.cn: 因为它以 -en 结尾，比较级用 more wooden。

normal.en: Woodenly adds -ly for the manner, woodenness adds -ness for the state.
normal.cn: woodenly 加 -ly 表示方式，woodenness 加 -ness 表示状态。

normal.en: A wooden face is a face like a board: flat, stiff, and giving nothing away.
normal.cn: wooden face 是像木板一样的脸：平坦、僵硬，什么都不透露。

abstract.en: A carved hand that cannot close its fingers.
abstract.cn: 一只雕好的手，手指合不上。

abstract.en: A door that opens with a long dry complaint.
abstract.cn: 一扇门打开时发出一声长长的干响。

abstract.en: A voice with no weather in it.
abstract.cn: 一个没有天气变化的声音。

examples.en: She stirred the soup with a wooden spoon and never let it boil.
examples.cn: 她用木勺搅着汤，从不让它滚起来。

examples.en: The dancer looked wooden because he was trying too hard.
examples.cn: 那位舞者显得僵硬，是因为他太使劲了。

examples.en: He answered in a wooden voice, like a person reading from a card.
examples.cn: 他生硬地回答，像在照着卡片念。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「屋登」——梯子是用木头做的，踩上去一级一级「噔」上去。

root: 古英语 wudu（木材）+ 后缀 -en（由……制成的，同 golden、silken）→ wooden；木不弯，故引申为「僵硬、呆板」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective begins as a statement about material, then moves to bodies that will not bend, then to faces and voices with no change in them.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词从说明材料开始，转到弯不了的身体，再转到毫无变化的脸和声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carved hand that cannot close.
core.cn: 核心意象：雕好却合不上手指的木手。

branches.en: The material branch: rows of wooden seats in a church.
branches.cn: 材料分支：教堂里一排排木椅。

branches.en: The body branch: stiff steps on the dance floor.
branches.cn: 身体分支：舞池里僵硬的舞步。

branches.en: The manner branch: a wooden performance.
branches.cn: 举止分支：呆板的表演。

branches.en: The everyday branch: wooden describes tools and acting alike.
branches.cn: 日常分支：wooden 既形容工具也形容表演。

branches.en: The stiffness branch: from limbs that will not bend to a voice that will not rise.
branches.cn: 僵硬分支：从弯不了的肢体到起伏不了的声音。

intro.en: Wooden is a stem plus one suffix; the ending -en is the part that says made of.
intro.cn: wooden 是一个词干加一个后缀；说「由……制成」的正是 -en。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are native and Germanic; the Latin words below express the same made-of idea with a different ending.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都是日耳曼语本土成分；下面的拉丁词用另一种词尾表达同样的「由……制成」。

items.exampleCN: 它由 wood 构成 wooden。

items.example: The suffix also builds wool words.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾也用于 wool 一族。

definition_zh: 羊毛；毛线；毛料；毛纺织品
definition_en: the soft thick hair of sheep and some other animals, or the yarn and cloth made from it
core_image: 一大团刚从羊身上剪下的毛，捏一把会慢慢弹回来
scene: 冬天到了，奶奶翻出那团一直没用完的毛线，开始给孙辈织围巾。This sweater is pure wool, so it stays warm even when it gets wet.
sceneCN: 这里 wool 是「羊毛、毛线」（第 1 个义项：羊身上柔软浓密的毛，也指用它纺成的线）；句意是这件毛衣是纯羊毛的，湿了也仍然暖和。捏一把会慢慢弹回来的毛团，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wool 加 -en 构成，义为「羊毛制的」
由 wool 加 -y 构成，义为「毛茸茸的；模糊的」
由 woolen 转作名词，义为「毛织品；毛料衣服」

senses.title: The fleece of the sheep
senses.definition: the soft thick hair that grows on sheep and some other animals, cut off once a year
senses.definitionCN: 羊及少数其他动物身上柔软浓密的毛，每年剪一次
senses.example: The farmer sells the wool from his sheep every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫每年春天卖掉羊身上的羊毛。
senses.why: This is the living source: the coat of the animal before anyone spins it.
senses.whyCN: 这是活的源头：还没被人纺过的动物皮毛。

senses.title: The spun thread
senses.definition: the yarn made by twisting the fibre, sold in balls for knitting
senses.definitionCN: 把纤维捻成的纱线，常以团为单位出售供编织
senses.example: Grandmother wound the wool into a ball before she started the scarf.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶先把毛线绕成团，才动手织围巾。
senses.why: Once the fibre is twisted, the same word follows it into the ball on the table.
senses.whyCN: 纤维一旦被捻成线，这个词就跟着它走进桌上那团线里。

senses.title: The woven cloth
senses.definition: the cloth woven from the yarn, used for coats and suits
senses.definitionCN: 用这种线织成的布料，用于外套和西装
senses.example: This sweater is pure wool, so it stays warm even when it gets wet.
senses.exampleCN: 这件毛衣是纯羊毛的，湿了也仍然暖和。
senses.why: From the ball to the loom is one more step, and the material name covers the finished cloth too.
senses.whyCN: 从线团到织机只差一步，材料名便也涵盖了织成的布。

senses.title: Being pulled back
senses.definition: used in the fixed phrase "pull the wool over someone's eyes", meaning to trick them
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定说法「pull the wool over someone's eyes」，意即欺骗某人
senses.example: He tried to pull the wool over her eyes, but she had checked the figures.
senses.exampleCN: 他想蒙骗她，但她早已核过数字。
senses.why: The soft fibre of a wig or a hood once hid the eyes, so the material stands for a blindfold.
senses.whyCN: 早年假发或兜帽的柔软毛料会遮住眼睛，于是这种材料成了蒙眼布的代称。

intro.en: Wool is Old English wull, shared with German Wolle and Dutch wol, and going back to a reconstructed root for the fleece.
intro.cn: wool 来自古英语 wull，与德语 Wolle、荷兰语 wol 同源，可上溯到一个表示羊毛的重构词根。

items.en: wull named the fleece of the sheep and the cloth made from it.
items.cn: wull 指羊的毛以及用它制成的布。

items.en: The same word for fleece appears across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 相同的「羊毛」一词出现在各门日耳曼语中。

items.en: The vowel shortened and the spelling settled on wool.
items.cn: 元音变短，拼写固定为 wool。

items.en: The endings -en and -y built woollen and woolly.
items.cn: 词尾 -en 与 -y 造出 woollen 与 woolly。

items.en: Idioms such as "pull the wool over someone's eyes" fixed the word in everyday speech.
items.cn: 「pull the wool over someone's eyes」之类的成语让这个词进入日常口语。

note.en: The first group holds the forms built on the same stem, the second holds other textile words that often meet it.
note.cn: 第一组收同根构成的词形，第二组收常与它相遇的其他纺织词。

entries.definition: Made of wool, British spelling.
Made of wool, the American spelling.
Soft and fuzzy, or unclear in outline.
The coat of wool on a sheep.
Thread spun from fibre for knitting.
The soft white fibre of the cotton plant.

normalIntro.en: Wool is a short native word with a doubled vowel spelling but a single short sound.
normalIntro.cn: wool 是一个简短的本土词，两个 o 只读一个短音。

normal.en: Two o letters, one short vowel sound: wool rhymes with full.
normal.cn: 两个 o 只读一个短元音：wool 与 full 押韵。

normal.en: Woollen and woolen are two spellings of the same adjective, British and American.
normal.cn: woollen 与 woolen 是同一个形容词的英式与美式拼写。

normal.en: Woolly doubles the l before -y; the other spelling keeps -en instead.
normal.cn: woolly 在 -y 前双写 l；另一种拼写则用 -en。

normal.en: Cotton wool is not wool at all, which shows how the word can mean soft fibre in general.
normal.cn: cotton wool 根本不是羊毛，可见这个词也可泛指柔软的纤维。

normal.en: The idiom "pull the wool over his eyes" comes from a soft cloth hiding the eyes.
normal.cn: 成语「pull the wool over his eyes」源自用软布遮眼。

abstract.en: A handful of fleece that slowly springs back into shape.
abstract.cn: 一把羊毛慢慢弹回原样。

abstract.en: The smell of a sweater dried near a fire.
abstract.cn: 在火边烘干的毛衣的气味。

abstract.en: A year of warmth carried in two hands.
abstract.cn: 一整年的温暖捧在两只手里。

examples.en: This coat is lined with thick wool for the winter.
examples.cn: 这件外套用厚羊毛做衬，适合冬天。

examples.en: She bought three balls of wool to knit a scarf.
examples.cn: 她买了三团毛线来织围巾。

examples.en: Nobody could pull the wool over his eyes after that mistake.
examples.cn: 出了那次错以后，谁也别想蒙他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捂」——冬天用羊毛把脖子捂得严严的。

root: 古英语 wull（羊毛），与德语 Wolle、荷兰语 wol 同源；-en 与 -y 分别构成 woollen、woolly。

sensesIntro.en: The fleece comes first, then the thread twisted from it, then the cloth woven from the thread, and finally the soft blindfold of an idiom.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是羊毛，再是捻成的线，接着是织成的布，最后是那句成语里的软蒙眼布。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a handful of fleece springing back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把会弹回来的羊毛。

branches.en: The source branch: wool sold from the farm each spring.
branches.cn: 源头分支：农场每年春天卖羊毛。

branches.en: The yarn branch: a ball of wool before knitting.
branches.cn: 纱线分支：织之前的线团。

branches.en: The cloth branch: a coat that stays warm when wet.
branches.cn: 布料分支：湿了也暖的外套。

branches.en: The trick branch: the soft cloth over the eyes.
branches.cn: 欺骗分支：遮在眼前的软布。

branches.en: The material branch: one word from the sheep to the coat.
branches.cn: 材料分支：一个词从羊到外套。

intro.en: Wool is a bare stem; -en and -y are the endings that turn it into adjectives.
intro.cn: wool 是裸词干；-en 与 -y 是把它变成形容词的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below name wool or fleece from another branch.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词从另一支来指羊毛。

items.example: It names the same coat before shearing.
items.exampleCN: 指剪毛前的同一层毛被。

items.example: It is the step before wool.
items.exampleCN: 它是羊毛之前的一道工序。

definition_zh: 词；单词；话；消息；诺言
definition_en: a single unit of language that has a meaning, or a short remark, news, or a promise
core_image: 一个人张开嘴，一个音节落出来，另一个人的表情立刻变了
scene: 母亲只轻轻说了两个字，站在门口的孩子就放下手里的东西转身回了屋。I did not catch a single word of what he said in the noisy hall.
sceneCN: 这里 word 是「词、说的话」（第 1 个义项：语言中能独立表意的最小单位）；句意是在嘈杂的大厅里我一句也没听清他说的话。一个音节落下、听者表情立刻改变，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 word 加 -y 构成，义为「话多的；冗长的」
由 word 加 -ing 构成，义为「措辞；用词」
由 word 加 -less 构成，义为「无言的；说不出话的」
由 word 与 play 复合，义为「文字游戏；双关」

senses.title: The unit of language
senses.definition: a single unit of speech or writing that carries a meaning of its own
senses.definitionCN: 口语或书面语中能独立承载意义的最小单位
senses.example: I did not catch a single word of what he said in the noisy hall.
senses.exampleCN: 在嘈杂的大厅里，他说的每一句话我都没听清。
senses.why: This is the literal core: one sound or one written group that stands for something.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的核心：一串声音或一组字母，代表某个东西。

senses.title: Something said
senses.definition: a remark or statement, often a short one, taken as it was spoken
senses.definitionCN: 说出口的话或陈述，常常较短，按原样取用
senses.example: A word from her was enough to quiet the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 她只说一句话，整个屋子就静了下来。
senses.why: Once a unit of language is spoken, it becomes an act in the world, so the word means the remark itself.
senses.whyCN: 语言单位一旦说出口，就成了世界中的一个动作，于是这个词也就指那句具体的话。

senses.title: News carried by speech
senses.definition: information passed from one person to another, usually in the phrase send word
senses.definitionCN: 从一人传到另一人的消息，常用于 send word 这一说法
senses.example: Word of the flood reached the village before the water did.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水的消息比水先到了村里。
senses.why: Because news travels by speech, the unit of speech came to stand for the news it carries.
senses.whyCN: 因为消息靠言语传递，说话的単位便代表它所承载的消息。

senses.title: A promise
senses.definition: a promise that one gives serious weight to, as in keep one's word
senses.definitionCN: 认真对待的承诺，如 keep one's word
senses.example: He gave his word that the work would be finished by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他保证这项活儿周五之前完成。
senses.why: A spoken promise is only words, so the word itself became the deposit for trust.
senses.whyCN: 说出口的承诺只是言语，于是这个词本身成了信任的抵押。

senses.title: The way something is put
senses.definition: the particular choice of words used to express something, as in the wording of a rule
senses.definitionCN: 表达某事时的具体用词选择，如条文的措辞
senses.example: The lawyer asked for a change in the word order of the clause.
senses.exampleCN: 律师要求改一下这一条款的词序。
senses.why: Where the unit of language is arranged and chosen, the word names the arrangement as well.
senses.whyCN: 语言单位被挑选与排列的地方，这个词便也指那种排列。

intro.en: Word is Old English word, shared with German Wort and Dutch woord, and originally meant a spoken utterance before it meant a unit of grammar.
intro.cn: word 来自古英语 word，与德语 Wort、荷兰语 woord 同源，最初指说出口的话语，后来才指语法单位。

items.en: word meant a spoken utterance or a message, not a unit on a page.
items.cn: word 指说出口的话或一条信息，不是纸上的一处单位。

items.en: The same noun appears in the other Germanic languages with the same sense.
items.cn: 同一名词在其他日耳曼语里出现，意思相同。

items.en: Latin verbum was the model for grammar writing, which helped the unit sense grow.
items.cn: 拉丁语 verbum 是语法写作的样板，帮助了「单位」这一义项的生长。

items.en: The spelling took its r after the vowel, and word was fixed in both senses, utterance and unit.
items.cn: 拼写把 r 放在元音之后，word 在「话语」与「单位」两义上固定下来。

items.en: The promise sense hardened in phrases such as keep one's word.
items.cn: 诺言之义在 keep one's word 之类的说法里凝定。

note.en: The first group holds the family of words built on this stem, the second holds other language units and speech terms.
note.cn: 第一组收由这个词干构成的词族，第二组收其他语言单位与言辞词。

entries.definition: More than one word, or remarks in general.
The way something is phrased.
Using too many words.
A word or phrase used for a special purpose.
A group of words that work together.
A complete unit of grammar with a subject and a verb.

normalIntro.en: Word is one syllable of old Germanic shape, and its promise sense lives entirely in phrases.
normalIntro.cn: word 是一个很短的日耳曼语音节，它的「诺言」义完全活在固定说法里。

normal.en: Four letters, one vowel sound: word is not spelled like world, so do not add an l.
normal.cn: 四个字母，一个元音：word 与 world 不同，不要多写一个 l。

normal.en: Word for word means exactly the same words, repeated in order.
normal.cn: word for word 指一字不改、照原样重复。

normal.en: In other words introduces a restatement, not a new idea.
normal.cn: in other words 引出换一种说法，而不是新想法。

normal.en: Keep one's word comes from the old idea that a spoken promise is a deposit.
normal.cn: keep one's word 来自「说出口的承诺就是抵押」的旧观念。

normal.en: Have a word with someone means a short talk, not a dictionary exercise.
normal.cn: have a word with someone 指简短谈一谈，不是查词典。

abstract.en: One syllable dropping into a room and changing every face.
abstract.cn: 一个音节落进屋里，每张脸都变了。

abstract.en: A promise left on the table like a coin.
abstract.cn: 一句诺言像硬币一样留在桌上。

abstract.en: Two small letters that carry a whole day of news.
abstract.cn: 两个小字母带着一整天的消息。

examples.en: I looked up the word in an old dictionary.
examples.cn: 我在一本旧词典里查了这个词。

examples.en: Please send word as soon as you arrive.
examples.cn: 你一到就请捎个信来。

examples.en: She kept her word and came back the next morning.
examples.cn: 她守信，第二天早上真的回来了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝的」——话是从心窝的，「词」也是从心里出来的。

root: 古英语 word（话语；言语），与德语 Wort、荷兰语 woord 同源；并非源自拉丁语，语法意义上的「词」在后世受 verbum 影响而加强。

sensesIntro.en: From one unit of language the meaning widens to what is said, then to news carried by speech, then to a promise, and finally to the way things are phrased.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个语言单位开始，意义扩展到说出的话、靠言语传递的消息、承诺，最后是措辞的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one syllable dropping into a room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个音节落进屋里。

branches.en: The unit branch: a word looked up in a dictionary.
branches.cn: 单位分支：在词典里查的词。

branches.en: The remark branch: a word that quiets a room.
branches.cn: 言语分支：一句话让屋子安静。

branches.en: The news branch: word of the flood arriving early.
branches.cn: 消息分支：先到的洪水消息。

branches.en: The promise branch: giving one's word by Friday.
branches.cn: 诺言分支：保证周五前完成。

branches.en: The style branch: from what is said to how it is put.
branches.cn: 文体分支：从说了什么到怎么说的。

intro.en: Word is a bare stem; the endings -y, -ing and -less build its family, and a few compounds widen it further.
intro.cn: word 是裸词干；-y、-ing、-less 造出词族，几个复合词进一步把它拓宽。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic with no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below name the same unit in the grammar tradition.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词是语法传统中对同一单位的称呼。

items.meaning: a set of keys for typing
items.example: It shows word forms compounding freely.
items.exampleCN: 可见 word 的词形自由构成复合词。

definition_zh: 工作；劳动；干活；运转；起作用；作品；著作
definition_en: to do a job, to labour, or to function properly; also the job itself or something made by effort
core_image: 一双手反复做同一个动作，桌上的东西一点点成形
scene: 车间的灯早上五点就亮了，老师傅已经站在台前擦过两遍手。My father has worked in the same factory for thirty years.
sceneCN: 这里 work 是「工作、干活」（第 1 个义项：为做事而付出劳动）；句意为我父亲在同一家工厂工作了三十年。一双手反复同一个动作、桌上东西慢慢成形，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 work 加 -er 构成，义为「工人；工作者」
由 work 加 -ing 构成，义为「工作的；运转中的」
由 work 加 -able 构成，义为「可行的；可运转的」
由 work 与 -aholic 拼合，义为「工作狂」

senses.title: To do a job
senses.definition: to spend effort on a task, especially in a job that earns money
senses.definitionCN: 为完成某项任务付出力气，尤指挣钱的工作
senses.example: My father has worked in the same factory for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 我父亲在同一家工厂工作了三十年。
senses.why: The oldest sense is effort put into something, whether paid or not.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是投入到某事上的力气，不论有没有报酬。

senses.title: To function well
senses.definition: to move or operate correctly, as a machine or a plan does
senses.definitionCN: 像机器或方案那样正确地运行
senses.example: The old radio still works if you turn the dial slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 慢慢转旋钮的话，那台旧收音机还能响。
senses.why: When effort succeeds, the thing made by it keeps going, so the word also means to run properly.
senses.whyCN: 力气奏效之后，被做出来的东西能持续运行，于是这个词也表示正常运转。

senses.title: The job itself
senses.definition: the activity or the post by which money is earned
senses.definitionCN: 用来挣钱的活动或职位
senses.example: She takes her work home with her almost every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她几乎每天晚上都把工作带回家。
senses.why: Here the noun stops naming the effort and names the post that keeps asking for it.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词不再指那份力气，而指不断要你去付出力气的那个职位。

senses.title: The thing made
senses.definition: a book, painting or other thing produced by effort and skill
senses.definitionCN: 靠努力与技巧做出的书、画或其他东西
senses.example: The painting is said to be the work of a young student.
senses.exampleCN: 据说这幅画是一位年轻学生的作品。
senses.why: The noun turns from the effort to whatever the effort leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 名词从付出的力气，转到力气留下的东西。

senses.title: To have an effect
senses.definition: to produce the effect that is wanted, as a medicine or a method does
senses.definitionCN: 产生预期的效果，如药物或方法
senses.example: The medicine worked better than the doctor had expected.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药的效力比大夫预想的还好。
senses.why: An effect that follows effort is the same idea as a machine running: something happens because of it.
senses.whyCN: 付出之后产生的效果，与机器运转是同一个想法：因为有了它，事情就发生了。

intro.en: Work is Old English weorc, meaning deed or labour, shared with German Werk and Greek ergon in the wider family.
intro.cn: work 来自古英语 weorc，意即行为或劳作，与德语 Werk 同源，更远可及希腊语 ergon。

items.en: weorc meant a deed and also the effort behind it.
items.cn: weorc 指一件作为，也指背后的付出。

items.en: The same noun and verb appear across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 同一名词与动词出现在各门日耳曼语中。

items.en: Norse forms such as verk reinforced the word in the north of England.
items.cn: verk 等北欧形式在英格兰北部强化了这个词。

items.en: The verb and the noun shared one spelling, which they still do.
items.cn: 动词与名词共用一个拼法，至今如此。

items.en: The result sense gave works, a word for books, music and pictures.
items.cn: 结果义造出 works，用来指书籍、音乐与绘画。

note.en: The first group holds the large family grown from this stem, the second holds other words for labour and for a produced thing.
note.cn: 第一组收由这个词干长出的庞大家族，第二组收其他表示劳动与成品的词。

entries.definition: A person who works, especially in a job.
Relating to work, or to a machine in use.
Possible to put into practice.
Physical work, often hard; British spelling.
A paid position or a particular task.
A piece of work that has to be done.

normalIntro.en: Work is one stem used as noun and verb, and its family grows with -er, -ing and -able.
normalIntro.cn: work 是同一个词干兼作名词与动词，词族靠 -er、-ing、-able 生长。

normal.en: Work is spelled with or, unlike walk, which has al.
normal.cn: work 中间是 or，而 walk 中间是 al。

normal.en: The noun and verb look the same; only the position in the sentence tells them apart.
normal.cn: 名词与动词写法相同，只能靠位置区分。

normal.en: Worker adds -er for a person, working adds -ing for a state.
normal.cn: worker 加 -er 指人，working 加 -ing 表状态。

normal.en: Work out has three senses: to calculate, to solve, and to exercise.
normal.cn: work out 有三义：算出、解决、锻炼。

normal.en: Works means a set of creations, as in the works of a poet.
normal.cn: works 指一系列创作，如某位诗人的作品。

abstract.en: A pair of hands repeating one motion until a shape appears.
abstract.cn: 一双手重复同一个动作，直到形状出现。

abstract.en: A lamp that stays on hours before anyone else comes in.
abstract.cn: 比谁都早亮的灯。

abstract.en: A radio dial turned very slowly to bring a voice back.
abstract.cn: 旋钮慢慢转，把声音找回来。

examples.en: She works in a small office near the station.
examples.cn: 她在车站附近一间小办公室工作。

examples.en: The plan will work only if everyone agrees.
examples.cn: 只有大家同意，这个方案才会奏效。

examples.en: This painting is the work of a young student.
examples.cn: 这幅画是一位年轻学生的作品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我克」——工作就是要一关一关地克过去。

root: 古英语 weorc（作为；劳作），与德语 Werk 同源，更远与希腊语 ergon（工作）同属一个古代词根体系。

sensesIntro.en: The effort comes first, then the job that pays, then running properly, then the thing produced, and finally the effect it has.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是付出的力气，再是挣钱的工作，接着是正常运转，然后是产出的东西，最后是它带来的效果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands repeating one motion until a shape appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手重复动作直到成形。

branches.en: The labour branch: thirty years in one factory.
branches.cn: 劳动分支：在一家厂干三十年。

branches.en: The machine branch: an old radio that still plays.
branches.cn: 机器分支：还能响的旧收音机。

branches.en: The career branch: taking the work home each night.
branches.cn: 职业分支：每晚把工作带回家。

branches.en: The creation branch: a painting by a student.
branches.cn: 创作分支：学生的画。

branches.en: The effect branch: something works because it changes an outcome.
branches.cn: 效果分支：起作用是因为改变了结果。

intro.en: Work is a bare stem with a very productive family: -er, -ing, -able and many compounds.
intro.cn: work 是裸词干，词族极其高产：-er、-ing、-able 以及大量复合词。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin words below belong to the same ancient labour family through a different branch.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语；下面的拉丁词经由另一支，同属古老「劳作」语族。

items.meaning: a room for making or teaching

definition_zh: 工人；工作者；雇员；工蜂；工蚁
definition_en: a person who does work, especially one employed in a job, or an insect such as a bee that does the work of the group
core_image: 清晨厂房门口一排安全帽，每个人的手上都有旧伤
scene: 厂门口的打卡机前，几个人一边排队一边咬着还没吃完的早点。The workers asked for safer machines after the accident last month.
sceneCN: 这里 worker 是「工人、雇员」（第 1 个义项：受雇做事的人）；句意为工人们要求在上个月的事故之后更换更安全的机器。清晨厂门口一排安全帽，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 工蜂；工蚁（群体中负责劳作的个体）

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -er 得到的动词，义为「工作；运转」
由 work 与 force 复合，义为「劳动力；全体员工」
由 worker 与 owned 复合，义为「工人所有的」

senses.title: The person who labours
senses.definition: a person who works, especially one who does physical or paid work
senses.definitionCN: 做事的人，尤指从事体力或受薪工作的人
senses.example: The workers asked for safer machines after the accident last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月的事故之后，工人们要求换成更安全的机器。
senses.why: The ending -er means the one who does, so the verb for labour becomes the name of a person.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -er 表示「做某事的人」，于是劳作的动词变成了人的称呼。

senses.title: The office employee
senses.definition: a person employed in an office, a service or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 在办公室、服务行业或专业领域受雇的人
senses.example: She is an office worker who commutes two hours each way.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个上班族，单程要通勤两个小时。
senses.why: The same doer ending works indoors too, so a desk job keeps the name of labour.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示行事者的词尾在室内也照样能用，于是坐办公桌的活仍带着「劳作」的名字。

senses.title: The insect that labours
senses.definition: a member of a bee or ant colony that does the collecting and building work
senses.definitionCN: 蜂群或蚁群中负责采集与建造的个体
senses.example: The workers of the hive carried pollen all day while the queen stayed inside.
senses.exampleCN: 蜂箱里的工蜂整天搬运花粉，蜂王留在里面。
senses.why: The name of a working person stretches to the insects whose whole life is work for the group.
senses.whyCN: 「劳作的人」这一称呼，延伸到一生都为群体劳作的昆虫身上。

intro.en: Worker is the Old English verb weorc plus the ending -er, which names the person who does the action.
intro.cn: worker 是古英语动词 weorc 加词尾 -er，用来称呼做这个动作的人。

items.en: The verb form was wyrcan, to do or to make, and the ending -ere named the doer.
items.cn: 动词形式是 wyrcan（做、造），词尾 -ere 指做事的人。

items.en: The ending weakened to -er, and the word settled as worker.
items.cn: 词尾弱化为 -er，这个词固定为 worker。

items.en: With the growth of factories the word became the everyday name of the employed.
items.cn: 随着工厂兴起，这个词成了受雇者的日常称呼。

items.en: The compound workforce appeared to name all the workers of a place together.
items.cn: 复合词 workforce 出现，用来统称一个地方的全部工人。

items.en: Natural history borrowed the word for the labouring members of a bee or ant colony.
items.cn: 博物学借这个词来指蜂群或蚁群中劳作的个体。

note.en: The first group holds the same stem in other shapes, the second holds other names for people who labour.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干的其他形态，第二组收其他称呼劳动者的词。

entries.definition: To labour, or the job itself.
More than one worker.
All the people who work in a place.
A person who does hard physical work.
A person hired to work for another.
All the people who work for an organisation.

normalIntro.en: Worker is work plus -er, the plainest pattern in English for turning an action into a person.
normalIntro.cn: worker 是 work 加 -er，是英语里把动作变成人的最朴素做法。

normal.en: The ending -er says the one who does, as in teacher and builder.
normal.cn: 词尾 -er 表示做某事的人，如 teacher 与 builder。

normal.en: Work plus er keeps every letter: worker, with no doubled consonant.
normal.cn: work 加 er 时每个字母都保留：worker，辅音不双写。

normal.en: Factory worker and office worker show the word needs a place to be exact.
normal.cn: factory worker 与 office worker 说明这个词需要地点来限定。

normal.en: A hard worker is not a strong worker: one praises effort, the other strength.
normal.cn: a hard worker 不等于 a strong worker：一个夸努力，一个说力气。

normal.en: The plural workers is also used for the whole class of employed people.
normal.cn: 复数 workers 也用来指整个受雇阶层。

abstract.en: A row of hard hats at the gate in early light.
abstract.cn: 晨光里门口一排安全帽。

abstract.en: A badge worn thin at one corner.
abstract.cn: 一枚一角磨薄的工牌。

abstract.en: Hands that know a tool better than a face.
abstract.cn: 一双手比一张脸更认得工具。

examples.en: The workers stopped for lunch at noon and sat on the steps.
examples.cn: 中午工人们停工吃饭，坐在台阶上。

examples.en: She is a careful worker who checks every page twice.
examples.cn: 她做事仔细，每一页都核对两遍。

examples.en: The workers in the hive never seem to rest.
examples.cn: 蜂巢里的工蜂好像从不休息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我克」加 -er：一个个难关都「克」过来的人，就是工人。

root: 古英语 wyrcan（做、造）+ 施事词尾 -ere → worker；与 work 同根，词族含 workforce、working。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the strong person who labours, widens to anyone employed, and then stretches to the insects that work for the colony.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从出力劳动的人开始，扩展到一切受雇者，再延伸到为群体劳作的昆虫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of hard hats at the factory gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：厂门口一排安全帽。

branches.en: The factory branch: workers asking for safer machines.
branches.cn: 工厂分支：要求更安全机器的工人。

branches.en: The office branch: a commuter two hours from home.
branches.cn: 办公室分支：通勤两小时的职员。

branches.en: The insect branch: bees carrying pollen all day.
branches.cn: 昆虫分支：整日搬运花粉的工蜂。

branches.en: The class branch: workers as a group with shared demands.
branches.cn: 阶层分支：作为群体的工人。

branches.en: The effort branch: the one who does the work of the whole.
branches.cn: 劳作分支：承担整个群体活儿的那一个。

intro.en: Worker is the simplest kind of derivative in English: a verb stem plus the agent ending -er.
intro.cn: worker 是英语里最简单的一种派生：动词词干加施事词尾 -er。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, but the agent ending has a Latin counterpart in -or, as in labourer's cousins.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，但施事词尾在拉丁语里对应 -or。

items.exampleCN: 它由 work 构成 worker。
它与 worker 并存为 working。

items.example: An older way to say the same.
The old word marked the sex.

definition_zh: 工匠；工人；技术工人
definition_en: a man who works with his hands in a trade, judged by the quality of his work
core_image: 一个钉子被敲三下正好齐平，不用再补
scene: 木器铺的老师傅做完一张凳子，用手掌沿边抹了一圈，确认没有毛刺。A good workman is known by the joints you cannot see.
sceneCN: 这里 workman 是「工匠、技术工人」（第 1 个义项：用手艺吃饭的人）；句意为好工匠凭的是你看不见的接缝来见本事。敲三下正好齐平的那颗钉子，就是这个词的印象。

collocations.phrase: a bad workman blames his tools

derivatives.zh: 由 workman 加 -ship 构成，义为「手艺；做工」
由 workman 加 -like 构成，义为「像工匠干出来的；干练的」
词根动词，义为「工作；干活」

senses.title: The hand that works
senses.definition: a man employed in a trade that calls for his hands and his skill
senses.definitionCN: 在需要手艺与双手的行业里受雇的男人
senses.example: The old workman raised the beam with three men and a rope.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老工匠带着三个人和一根绳子把横梁抬了起来。
senses.why: The compound joins work with man in its old sense of person, so it names a person whose life is the work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 work 与旧义为「人」的 man 结合，指以工作为生的人。

senses.title: The standard of the craft
senses.definition: the quality shown by what such a person makes, in phrases like a good workman
senses.definitionCN: 由此人做出来的东西体现的手艺水准，如 a good workman
senses.example: A good workman is known by the joints you cannot see.
senses.exampleCN: 好工匠凭你看不见的接缝来见本事。
senses.why: Here the word stops naming a person and names the standard that the person meets.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词不再指人，而指此人所达到的那条手艺标准。

senses.title: The one who blames the tool
senses.definition: used in the saying that a bad workman blames his tools, meaning skill matters more than equipment
senses.definitionCN: 用于谚语「a bad workman blames his tools」，意即本事比工具更重要
senses.example: When the shelf came out crooked he blamed the saw, but a bad workman blames his tools.
senses.exampleCN: 架子做得歪了，他便怪那把锯子，可是手笨的人才怨工具。
senses.why: A word for the skilled hand easily becomes part of a saying about the unskilled one.
senses.whyCN: 一个指巧手的词，很容易就成了一句话里指笨手的部分。

intro.en: Workman joins Old English weorc, work, with mann, a person; only much later did man narrow to males.
intro.cn: workman 由古英语 weorc（劳作）与 mann（人）结合；man 很晚才收窄为只指男性。

items.en: weorc and mann could combine freely, and the compound named a person who labours.
items.cn: weorc 与 mann 能自由组合，复合词用来指劳作的人。

items.en: Spelling settled as workman, and the trade sense grew with the guilds.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 workman，随着行会兴起了行业手艺之义。

items.en: The word became the mark of a man judged by the finish of his work.
items.cn: 这个词成了以成品好坏来评断的人的标记。

items.en: The suffix -ship built workmanship for the skill itself.
items.cn: 后缀 -ship 造出 workmanship 来指手艺本身。

items.en: In current use worker is far more common, and workman survives mostly in trade and proverb.
items.cn: 今天 worker 更常用，workman 主要留在行业语与谚语中。

note.en: The first group holds the same stem and its compounds, the second holds other names for a skilled hand.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干及其复合词，第二组收其他指手艺人的称呼。

entries.definition: More than one workman.
The skill shown in what is made.
Done in a competent, solid way.
A person skilled in a craft.
A person who repairs and maintains machines.
A skilled worker who makes things by hand in small numbers.

normalIntro.en: Workman is work plus man, and it keeps the old man that meant person, not male.
normalIntro.cn: workman 是 work 加 man，这里的 man 仍是「人」，不是「男人」。

normal.en: The plural is workmen, with a vowel change and no second e.
normal.cn: 复数是 workmen，元音变化且不再多加 e。

normal.en: Workmanship adds -ship for the skill, not for the person.
normal.cn: workmanship 加 -ship 指手艺，不是指人。

normal.en: The proverb about a bad workman blaming his tools is the phrase you will meet most.
normal.cn: 最常见的是那句「手笨怨工具」的谚语。

normal.en: Worker has largely replaced workman in normal writing.
normal.cn: 在一般写作中 worker 已基本取代 workman。

normal.en: Workmanlike means solid rather than brilliant: good, plain, finished.
normal.cn: workmanlike 指扎实而非出色：好、朴素、做完了。

abstract.en: A nail driven in three strokes, exactly flush.
abstract.cn: 三下敲平的一颗钉子。

abstract.en: A palm run along an edge to feel for rough grain.
abstract.cn: 手掌沿边抹过，感觉有没有毛刺。

abstract.en: Joints you cannot see holding the whole frame.
abstract.cn: 看不见的接缝撑住整个框架。

examples.en: The workmen finished the roof before the rain came.
examples.cn: 工匠们在雨来之前把屋顶修完了。

examples.en: The table shows the workmanship of an older generation.
examples.cn: 这张桌子显出上一代人的手艺。

examples.en: A bad workman blames his tools, my grandfather used to say.
examples.cn: 我爷爷常说，手笨的人才怨工具。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我克门」——一扇一扇门都靠我克出来的人，就是工匠。

root: 古英语 weorc（劳作）+ mann（人）→ workman；-ship 构成 workmanship（手艺），-like 构成 workmanlike。

sensesIntro.en: The person comes first, then the quality of what he makes, and finally the proverb about the one who blames his tools.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是指人，再是此人做成之物的品质，最后是那句关于怨工具之人的谚语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nail driven in exactly flush.
core.cn: 核心意象：钉子敲得正好齐平。

branches.en: The trade branch: workmen lifting a beam by rope.
branches.cn: 行业分支：用绳抬梁的工匠。

branches.en: The craft branch: joints that hold without showing.
branches.cn: 手艺分支：看不出却撑得住的接缝。

branches.en: The proverb branch: blaming the saw for a crooked shelf.
branches.cn: 谚语分支：架子歪了怪锯子。

branches.en: The reputation branch: a worker known by his finish.
branches.cn: 名声分支：以成品见本事的工人。

branches.en: The judgement branch: skill is praised or blamed by results.
branches.cn: 评断分支：本事靠结果被夸奖或责怪。

intro.en: Workman is a compound of two native words, and the endings -ship and -like build its two adjectives and nouns.
intro.cn: workman 是两个本土词的复合，-ship 与 -like 造出它的名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin; the words below belong to other languages that also name a skilled hand.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都不是拉丁语；下面的词属其他语言，同样指有手艺的人。

items.exampleCN: 它给出 workmen 而非 workmans。

items.example: It builds craftsmanship in some uses.
items.exampleCN: 有些用法中由它构成 craftsmanship。

definition_zh: 车间；作坊；研讨会；工作坊
definition_en: a room or building where things are made or repaired, or a short class where people work together on a subject
core_image: 一张长桌，工具挂在墙上排成一行，木屑落进沟槽里
scene: 学校的旧仓库被清出来，一半摆了台锯，一半摆了椅子。The workshop on writing lasted all Saturday morning and everyone left with a draft.
sceneCN: 这里 workshop 是「车间、工作坊」（第 1 个义项：制作或修理东西的房间）；句意为那个写作工作坊办了一整个周六上午，每个人走时都带着初稿。工具挂成一排的长桌，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 研讨会；工作坊（短期集体研习）

derivatives.zh: 第一成分，义为「工作」
第二成分，义为「店铺；工场」
由 workshop 加 -er 构成，义为「工作坊参与者」

senses.title: The room where things are made
senses.definition: a room or building with tools where goods are made or repaired
senses.definitionCN: 备有工具、用来制作或修理物品的房间或建筑
senses.example: The carpenter keeps his tools in a small workshop behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 木匠把工具放在屋后一个小作坊里。
senses.why: Shop once meant a place where work is done, so the compound simply says the place of working.
senses.whyCN: shop 原指干活的地方，因此这个复合词直接就是「干活之处」。

senses.title: A place of repair
senses.definition: a garage or small business that repairs machines or vehicles
senses.definitionCN: 修理机器或车辆的车库或小店
senses.example: The bus went back to the workshop with a broken door.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆公交因车门坏了开回了修理车间。
senses.why: Repair is making in reverse, so a garage keeps the name of the place where things are made.
senses.whyCN: 修理是倒过来的制作，于是修车的车库也沿用了「制作之处」这个名字。

senses.title: The shared study
senses.definition: a short session where a small group learns by doing and discussing together
senses.definitionCN: 小群体边做边讨论来学习的短期课程
senses.example: The workshop on writing lasted all Saturday morning and everyone left with a draft.
senses.exampleCN: 那个写作工作坊办了一整个周六上午，每个人走时都带着初稿。
senses.why: The meaning moved from the room where things are made to the meeting where ideas are made together.
senses.whyCN: 意义从「制作东西的房间」挪到了「一起做出想法的聚会」。

senses.title: The room of ideas
senses.definition: a meeting of specialists who work on one problem or draft
senses.definitionCN: 专家聚在一起处理某一问题或稿件的会议
senses.example: A workshop of six teachers produced the new course plan in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 六位老师组成的研习会两天就做出了新课程方案。
senses.why: When experts join hands on one problem, the meeting itself is a workshop where the plan is made.
senses.whyCN: 当专家为一件事携手时，这场会本身就是一个把方案做出来的车间。

intro.en: Workshop joins work with shop, a word that first meant a place where work is done, not a place that sells.
intro.cn: workshop 是 work 与 shop 的复合，shop 最初指干活的地方，而不是卖东西的地方。

items.en: weorc meant labour, and the word for a working place grew from it.
items.cn: weorc 指劳作，表示劳动场所的词由此而生。

items.en: A workshop was the room where a craft was carried out.
items.cn: workshop 指进行手艺活的房间。

items.en: With factories the word widened to any building of machines and benches.
items.cn: 随着工厂出现，这个词扩展到任何有机器和长台的建筑。

items.en: Teachers borrowed it for a short course where students work, not listen.
items.cn: 教师借用它，指学生动手而非只听讲的短期课程。

items.en: The sense of meeting to produce something together is now very common.
items.cn: 聚在一起共同做出成果的这个义项如今非常常见。

note.en: The first group holds compounds sharing the second element, the second holds other places and events of work.
note.cn: 第一组收与它共用后一部分的复合词，第二组收其他工作场所与活动。

entries.definition: A place of trade, or a place of work.
Labour, or a job.
The working area inside a workshop.
A room where an artist or maker works.
A class or meeting for discussion of a subject.
A building where goods are made in large numbers.

normalIntro.en: Workshop is two very common words joined, and the second one has shifted from place of work to meeting.
normalIntro.cn: workshop 是两个极常见词的复合，后半部分从「干活的地方」挪到了「聚会」。

normal.en: Shop here is not a store; the old sense is a place where work is done.
normal.cn: 这里的 shop 不是商店，旧义是干活的地方。

normal.en: Keep both halves when writing: workshop, with no hyphen in current use.
normal.cn: 两半都要写全：workshop，现今不加连字符。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s: workshops.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：workshops。

normal.en: A writing workshop works with drafts, not with wood, which shows the figure at work.
normal.cn: 写作工作坊用的是草稿而不是木头，可见这个比喻怎么运作。

normal.en: Attend or run a workshop: the verb pair follows the event sense.
normal.cn: attend a workshop 或 run a workshop，动词搭配跟着活动义走。

abstract.en: Sawdust settled in the groove of a long bench.
abstract.cn: 木屑落进长台的沟槽里。

abstract.en: Chairs pulled into a circle around a half-finished plan.
abstract.cn: 椅子围成一圈，中间是半成品方案。

abstract.en: Two rooms that share one idea of making.
abstract.cn: 两个房间共享一个「做」的想法。

examples.en: The car has been in the workshop for three days.
examples.cn: 这辆车在修理厂放了三天。

examples.en: The teacher runs a small workshop on speaking in public.
examples.cn: 这位老师主持一个小型的公开演讲工作坊。

examples.en: Dust covered every surface of the workshop by the end of the week.
examples.cn: 到周末，车间每处表面都是灰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝可学」——车间里窝着就能学到手艺。

root: work（劳作）+ shop（旧义「干活的地方」）→ workshop；后引申为「工作坊、研讨会」。

sensesIntro.en: The room of craft comes first, then the room of repair, then the meeting where ideas are made in the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是手艺的房间，再是修理的房间，接着是用同样方式做出来自想法的聚会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tools hanging in a row above a long bench.
core.cn: 核心意象：长台上面挂成一排的工具。

branches.en: The craft branch: a carpenter's small workshop.
branches.cn: 手艺分支：木匠的小作坊。

branches.en: The repair branch: a bus back with a broken door.
branches.cn: 修理分支：车门坏了回厂的车。

branches.en: The class branch: a Saturday writing workshop.
branches.cn: 课程分支：周六的写作工作坊。

branches.en: The specialist branch: six teachers drafting a course.
branches.cn: 专家分支：六位老师起草课程。

branches.en: The making branch: both rooms are places where something is made.
branches.cn: 制作分支：两种场景都是做出东西的地方。

intro.en: Workshop is a plain compound of two native words, with no living suffix at all.
intro.cn: workshop 是两个本土语的简单复合，完全没有活的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Neither element is Latin; the words below were borrowed from Latin for the same places of work.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都不是拉丁语；下面的词是从拉丁语借来表示同样工作场所的。

items.meaning: a place of working or trade

items.example: A word of Latin origin for the same idea.
items.exampleCN: 同义而源自拉丁语的词。
它构成 laboratory 与 factory。

items.example: Latin seed, now the nearest word to sense 03.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语的种子，如今最接近第 3 义。

definition_zh: 世界；地球；世人；领域；……界；世道
definition_en: the earth and everything on it, all people, or a particular area of activity and interest
core_image: 从很远处看下来，一整片陆地上灯火连成一条线
scene: 地图铺在桌上，孩子的指尖从一个国家滑到另一个国家，最后停在海边。He travelled the world before he settled down in a small town.
sceneCN: 这里 world 是「世界」（第 1 个义项：地球及其上的一切）；句意为他在一个小镇安顿下来之前走遍了世界。从远处看下去、灯火连成一线的大片陆地，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 world 加 -ly 构成，义为「尘世的；世俗的」
由 world 与 wide 复合，义为「全世界的」
由 world 与 view 复合，义为「世界观」
由 new 与 world 复合，义为「新大陆的」

senses.title: The earth and all on it
senses.definition: the earth together with its people, animals and places
senses.definitionCN: 地球及其上的人、动物与地方
senses.example: He travelled the world before he settled down in a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 他在小镇安顿下来之前走遍了世界。
senses.why: The old compound meant the age of man, and from there it came to name the whole place where people live.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老的复合词原意是「人的世代」，由此转而指人生活的整个场所。

senses.title: Everyone alive
senses.definition: all the people of the earth taken together
senses.definitionCN: 地球上全体的人合起来
senses.example: She told the world about the problem and the letters poured in.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这个问题说给了世人，信件便如潮水般涌来。
senses.why: The place here is not land but people, so the word stands for everyone alive at once.
senses.whyCN: 这里的场所不是土地而是人，于是这个词一下子指所有在世的人。

senses.title: The area of a subject
senses.definition: a particular field of work or interest with its own rules and people
senses.definitionCN: 有一定规则、人物与关注点的特定领域
senses.example: He is well known in the world of science.
senses.exampleCN: 他在科学界很有名。
senses.why: A wide place shrinks to one enclosed circle of people who share a trade, and the same word serves.
senses.whyCN: 一片广阔地方缩小成同行相聚的一个圈子，用的还是同一个词。

senses.title: The way things are
senses.definition: the circumstances of human life, often with a tone of experience or complaint
senses.definitionCN: 人生活的境况，常带阅历或无奈的口吻
senses.example: They have seen enough of the world to know what to expect.
senses.exampleCN: 他们见过的世事足够多，知道该期待什么。
senses.why: When the place sense is used figuratively, it names the span of human affairs rather than a location.
senses.whyCN: 当「场所」义被比喻使用时，它指人间事务的跨度，而不是一个地点。

intro.en: World comes from Old English weorold, a compound of wer, man, and eld, age, so its first sense was the age of man.
intro.cn: world 来自古英语 weorold，由 wer（人）与 eld（世代）复合，最初的意思是「人的世代」。

items.en: weorold meant the age or course of human life, then the whole setting of it.
items.cn: weorold 指人的世代或人生历程，后来指其整个环境。

items.en: The parts wer, man, and eld, age, are Germanic and still visible in werewolf.
items.cn: wer（人）与 eld（世代）属日耳曼语，在 werewolf 中仍可见其痕迹。

items.en: The two parts fused, the r moved, and the word settled toward world.
items.cn: 两部分融合，r 的位置移动，词形固定为 world。

items.en: The place sense widened while the man sense faded from memory.
items.cn: 「场所」义扩大，而「人」的意思从记忆中淡去。

items.en: The field-of-interest sense arose in phrases such as the world of art.
items.cn: 「领域」义兴起于 the world of art 之类的说法。

note.en: The first group holds compounds and derivatives built on this stem, the second holds other words for the planet and for spheres of activity.
note.cn: 第一组收由这个词干构成的复合词与派生词，第二组收其他指星球与活动圈子的词。

entries.definition: Concerned with ordinary life, not with the spirit.
Found or happening all over the earth.
A person's basic view of life.
The planet we live on.
The earth as a round body, or a model of it.
An area of activity or knowledge.

normalIntro.en: World is an old compound that fused into one word, and it has an l that word does not have.
normalIntro.cn: world 是一个融合成一词的古老复合词，它比 word 多一个 l。

normal.en: World has an l before the d; word does not, so check the spelling.
normal.cn: world 在 d 前有一个 l，word 没有，注意拼写。

normal.en: It once said the age of man, which is why it means the whole setting of life.
normal.cn: 它原指人的世代，所以指整个生活的场景。

normal.en: Worldly adds -ly for the earthly side, in contrast to the spiritual.
normal.cn: worldly 加 -ly 指尘世的一面，与精神相对。

normal.en: Worldwide joins wide, so the two ends of the earth are both included.
normal.cn: worldwide 与 wide 结合，把大地两端都包含在内。

normal.en: A world of difference means a huge contrast, not a geography lesson.
normal.cn: a world of difference 指巨大差别，不是地理课。

abstract.en: Lights joined into one line seen from very high up.
abstract.cn: 从极高处看，灯火连成一线。

abstract.en: A finger sliding across a map and stopping at the sea.
abstract.cn: 手指在地图上滑过，停在海边。

abstract.en: A room that holds only one subject but feels complete.
abstract.cn: 只装一个主题却像完整的房间。

examples.en: People all over the world watched the game.
examples.cn: 全世界的人都在看那场比赛。

examples.en: It made a world of difference to have someone to talk to.
examples.cn: 有个人能说说话，情况就大不一样。

examples.en: She is a rising name in the world of design.
examples.cn: 她是设计界冉冉升起的一个名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我的」——整个世界，归根到底是「我的」脚下这一块。

root: 古英语 weorold = wer（人）+ eld（世代），原义「人的世代」，后指人生活的整个世界；与 werewolf 的 were 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The age of man comes first, then the whole earth, then all people, then a single field, and finally the way life goes.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是人的世代，再是整片大地，接着是所有人，然后是一个领域，最后是生活的样子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lights joined into one line seen from far above.
core.cn: 核心意象：从高处看灯火连成一线。

branches.en: The earth branch: travelling the world before settling down.
branches.cn: 大地分支：安顿前走遍世界。

branches.en: The people branch: telling the world about a problem.
branches.cn: 人分支：把问题说给世人。

branches.en: The field branch: a name in the world of design.
branches.cn: 领域分支：设计界的名字。

branches.en: The experience branch: seeing enough of the world to expect trouble.
branches.cn: 阅历分支：见够了世事知道会有难处。

branches.en: The scale branch: from the planet to a small circle of experts.
branches.cn: 尺度分支：从星球到一小圈专家。

intro.en: World is an old fused compound; -ly and -wide are the endings its derivatives use.
intro.cn: world 是一个古老融合的复合词；它的派生词用 -ly 与 -wide 等词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, not Latin; the words below name the same planet from another tradition.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，不是拉丁语；下面的词从另一传统来指同一颗星球。

items.example: The whole compound as one word.
It gives worlds, as in other worlds.

definition_zh: 虫；蠕虫；蚯蚓；蠕动着前进；逐步套取（消息）
definition_en: a small soft creature with a long thin body and no legs, or to move slowly by twisting like one
core_image: 一块翻开的湿土里，一条细长的身体一缩一伸地往前移
scene: 雨后的小路上，几条蚯蚓被水冲出来，在石头上慢慢扭。The dog wormed its way under the gate and was gone before anyone noticed.
sceneCN: 这里 worm 是「虫、蠕虫」（第 1 个义项：身体细长柔软、没有腿的小生物）；句意为那条狗从大门底下钻了过去，谁也没注意到它就没了影。湿土里一缩一伸的细长身体，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 worm 加 -y 构成，义为「多虫的；虫蛀的」
由 worm 加 -like 构成，义为「像虫的；细长的」
由 silk 与 worm 复合，义为「蚕」

senses.title: The legless creature
