senses.definition: a small soft animal with a long thin body and no legs, living in soil or water
senses.definitionCN: 身体细长柔软、没有腿的小动物，生活在土里或水中
senses.example: After the rain the worms came up and lay on the path.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后虫子钻出土来，躺在小路上。
senses.why: This is the creature itself, the shape of which drives every other sense.
senses.whyCN: 这就是这种生物本身，它的形状驱动了其余所有义项。

senses.title: To move like one
senses.definition: to move slowly and with difficulty by twisting the body close to the ground
senses.definitionCN: 贴着地扭动身体，缓慢艰难地移动
senses.example: The dog wormed its way under the gate and was gone before anyone noticed.
senses.exampleCN: 那条狗从大门底下钻了过去，谁也没注意到它就没影了。
senses.why: The verb borrows the body's way of travelling: no legs, no hurry, just twisting forward.
senses.whyCN: 动词借用了这种身体的走法：没有腿，也不急，只是一路扭过去。

senses.title: To pull secrets out bit by bit
senses.definition: to get information out of someone slowly and indirectly, as in worm something out of someone
senses.definitionCN: 慢慢间接地从他人那里取得消息，如 worm something out of someone
senses.example: It took her an hour to worm the truth out of him.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了一个小时才从他嘴里套出实情。
senses.why: Wriggling into a narrow place is exactly how one gets into another person's confidence step by step.
senses.whyCN: 往窄缝里慢慢钻，正是人一步步钻进别人心事里的样子。

senses.title: The wretched person
senses.definition: a mean and contemptible person, used as a word of low abuse
senses.definitionCN: 卑劣可鄙的人，用作轻蔑的骂词
senses.example: Nobody trusted the worm who had sold the plans to a rival.
senses.exampleCN: 没人信任那个把图纸卖给对手的可鄙家伙。
senses.why: A creature that lives by creeping and twisting easily becomes a picture of a person who betrays.
senses.whyCN: 靠钻营扭动过活的生物，很容易变成背叛者的画像。

senses.title: The one who turns at last
senses.definition: used in the saying the worm turns, meaning even the most patient person will resist
senses.definitionCN: 用于谚语 the worm turns，意即最忍让的人也会反抗
senses.example: He said nothing for years, and then the worm turned.
senses.exampleCN: 他多年不作声，后来终于翻脸了。
senses.why: Even a body with no strength can turn, and that turning is the proverb's whole point.
senses.whyCN: 就连毫无力气的身体也能扭过来，这个「扭」就是整句谚语的要点。

intro.en: Worm is Old English wyrm, which first meant a serpent, and only later narrowed to the small creatures of soil.
intro.cn: worm 来自古英语 wyrm，最初指蛇，后来才收窄为土里的小虫。

items.en: wyrm meant a snake or a dragon, the long bending body, not the small soil creature.
items.cn: wyrm 指蛇或龙，是那细长扭动的身体，并非土中小虫。

items.en: The same word for serpent appears in Norse and German forms.
items.cn: 表示蛇的同一词出现在北欧与德语的形式中。

items.en: Latin vermis, a worm, lived beside it in learned writing and reinforced the small-creature sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vermis（虫）在学术写作中与之并存，强化了小虫之义。

items.en: The meaning narrowed to small soft creatures, while dragon survived only in old poetry.
items.cn: 词义收窄为柔软的小生物，龙义仅存于古诗。

items.en: The verb grew out of the creature's way of moving, and then out of its way of getting in.
items.cn: 动词先由它移动的方式长出来，再延伸到它钻进去的方式。

note.en: The first group holds the derived forms, the second holds other small creatures that people confuse it with.
note.cn: 第一组收派生形式，第二组收容易与它混淆的其他小生物。

entries.definition: More than one worm.
Full of worms, or eaten by them.
The caterpillar that spins silk.
A small creature with six legs and a body in three parts.
A long thin animal with no legs and scales.
The wormlike young of a butterfly or moth.

normalIntro.en: Worm is a short old word whose first meaning was snake, and whose shape still drives its metaphors.
normalIntro.cn: worm 是一个短小的古词，最初指蛇，它的形状至今驱动着各种比喻。

normal.en: Worm rhymes with term, and unlike warm it keeps a short crisp vowel.
normal.cn: worm 与 term 押韵，与 warm 不同，元音短而紧。

normal.en: The first meaning was snake, so a worm in old texts may be something larger.
normal.cn: 最初义是蛇，所以旧文本里的 worm 可能是个更大的东西。

normal.en: Silkworm and tapeworm show the word joining with another to name a kind.
normal.cn: silkworm 与 tapeworm 显示它与另一词结合来指某一类。

normal.en: Worm out of means pull out slowly, like a thread pulled by twisting.
normal.cn: worm out of 指慢悠悠地拽出来，像扭着拉一根线。

normal.en: The worm turns comes from the idea that even a soft body will finally wriggle free.
normal.cn: the worm turns 源自「再软的身体最后也会扭开」的想象。

abstract.en: A thin body folding and unfolding through wet soil.
abstract.cn: 细长的身体在湿土里一折一伸。

abstract.en: A shape with no eyes, no legs, and no pause.
abstract.cn: 一个没有眼睛、没有腿、也不停下的形状。

abstract.en: A body that moves by giving up its own straightness.
abstract.cn: 一个靠放弃笔直而前进的身体。

examples.en: The child put the worm back into the soil gently.
examples.cn: 孩子轻轻把蚯蚓放回土里。

examples.en: He wormed through the narrow gap behind the shelf.
examples.cn: 他从架子后面的窄缝里挤了过去。

examples.en: She wormed the whole story out of her brother at dinner.
examples.cn: 晚饭时她把整件事从弟弟嘴里套了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我摸」——土里一摸，摸到一条软软的虫。

root: 古英语 wyrm（蛇；龙），与德语、北欧语同源；拉丁语 vermis（虫）在后世加强「小虫」义。

sensesIntro.en: The creature comes first, then its way of moving, then its way of creeping into secrets, then the abuse, and finally the revolt.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是这种生物，再是它移动的样子，接着是它钻进秘密的方式，然后是骂人语，最后是反抗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin body folding through wet soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿土里一折一伸的细长身体。

branches.en: The creature branch: worms lying on the path after rain.
branches.cn: 生物分支：雨后躺在路上的虫。

branches.en: The movement branch: a dog wriggling under the gate.
branches.cn: 移动分支：从门下钻过的狗。

branches.en: The secret branch: pulling the truth out slowly.
branches.cn: 秘密分支：慢慢套出实情。

branches.en: The abuse branch: the one who sold the plans.
branches.cn: 骂词分支：卖图纸的那个人。

branches.en: The revolt branch: silence that finally breaks.
branches.cn: 反抗分支：终于打破的沉默。

intro.en: Worm is a bare stem; -y and -like build adjectives, and compounds name whole families of creatures.
intro.cn: worm 是裸词干；-y 与 -like 构成形容词，复合词则命名一整类生物。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, but Latin vermis lived beside it and left its own traces, such as vermin.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，但拉丁语 vermis 与之并存，并留下了 vermin 之类的痕迹。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 vermin 与 vermicelli。

definition_zh: 担心；担忧；使担心；焦虑；烦恼
definition_en: to feel anxious about something, to make someone anxious, or the feeling of anxiety itself
core_image: 半夜翻来覆去，同一件事在脑子里绕圈，越绕越紧
scene: 离考试还有三天，她已经把同一页笔记看了五遍，却什么也没记住。Do not worry; the letter will arrive in a day or two.
sceneCN: 这里 worry 是「担心」（第 1 个义项：对未定之事感到不安）；句意为别担心，信一两天就到。半夜翻来覆去、同一件事在脑子里绕圈，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 worry 加 -ed 构成，义为「担心的；焦虑的」
由 worry 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人担忧的」
由 worrying 加 -ly 构成，义为「令人担忧地」
由 worry 与 wart 拼合，义为「爱操心的人」

senses.title: To feel anxious
senses.definition: to keep turning over something uncertain or unpleasant in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 心里反复想着未定或不好的事
senses.example: Do not worry; the letter will arrive in a day or two.
senses.exampleCN: 别担心，信一两天就到。
senses.why: The oldest meaning is to strangle, and the mind does to a thought what a hand does to a throat.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是勒住，而心对念头做的事，正如手对喉咙做的事。

senses.title: To make someone anxious
senses.definition: to cause another person to feel uneasy by what one does
senses.definitionCN: 因自己的行为让别人感到不安
senses.example: It worries me that she has not called since Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 她周五之后就没来电话，这让我不安。
senses.why: The same grip is now given to another person, so the verb moves from feeling it to causing it.
senses.whyCN: 同一只手现在攥住的是别人，于是动词从「被攥」变为「去攥」。

senses.title: The feeling
senses.definition: the state of being anxious, or a particular thing that causes it
senses.definitionCN: 焦虑的状态，或引起它的一件件具体事
senses.example: Money is the biggest worry for most families this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年大多数家庭最大的烦恼就是钱。
senses.why: The verb turns into a noun that names both the state and the things that keep it going.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成名词，既指那种状态，也指不断维持它的那些事。

senses.title: To keep biting at something
senses.definition: of an animal, to bite and shake something again and again
senses.definitionCN: 指动物反复咬住并甩动某物
senses.example: The dog worried the old shoe until the sole came off.
senses.exampleCN: 那只狗把那旧鞋咬来甩去，直到鞋底脱落。
senses.why: This is the oldest visible sense: the throat, the bite, the grip that does not let go.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的可见义：喉咙、咬住、不放的那只手。

intro.en: Worry came from Old English wyrgan, to strangle, and only in modern English did it come to mean mental distress.
intro.cn: worry 来自古英语 wyrgan（勒死），到近代英语才用于表示心里的忧苦。

items.en: wyrgan meant to strangle or to seize by the throat.
items.cn: wyrgan 意为勒死或扼住喉咙。

items.en: The stem appears in other Germanic words for choking and wrestling.
items.cn: 同一词干出现在其他日耳曼语中表示窒息与扭打的词里。

items.en: The meaning moved to seizing and shaking with the teeth, as a dog worries a bone.
items.cn: 词义转向用牙齿咬住甩动，如狗折腾骨头。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the sense spread to the mind: to worry a problem.
items.cn: 十九世纪这层意思扩展到内心：把一个问题反复「咬住」。

items.en: The anxious sense became the main one, and the earlier bite sense survives in descriptions of animals.
items.cn: 忧虑义成了主要义项，早先的咬义仅存于描述动物的文字中。

note.en: The first group holds the forms of the same verb, the second holds other words for anxiety.
note.cn: 第一组收同一动词的各种形态，第二组收其他表示焦虑的词。

entries.definition: Feeling anxious.
Causing anxiety.
Third person singular, or more than one worry.
A feeling of worry about someone or something.
A stronger, often lasting feeling of worry.
To worry in a small, restless way.

normalIntro.en: Worry keeps the stem and changes y to i before endings: worries, worried.
normalIntro.cn: worry 保留词干，在加词尾时把 y 变成 i：worries、worried。

normal.en: After a consonant plus y, the y turns to i before -es and -ed: worried.
normal.cn: 辅音加 y 结尾，接 -es、-ed 时 y 变 i：worried。

normal.en: The present participle adds -ing without a change: worrying.
normal.cn: 现在分词直接加 -ing：worrying。

normal.en: Worry about takes the thing that troubles you, worry over is a more literary variant.
normal.cn: worry about 后接让你发愁的事，worry over 更书面。

normal.en: The verb can take a person as object: it worries me, meaning it makes me anxious.
normal.cn: 这个动词也可以接人作宾语：it worries me，意思是他让我担心。

normal.en: Its old meaning is to strangle, which explains why worry feels like a grip on the chest.
normal.cn: 它的古义是勒住，这解释了担心为何像胸口被攥住。

abstract.en: A thought circling the same night hour after hour.
abstract.cn: 一个念头一夜又一夜地绕圈。

abstract.en: A hand closing, though there is nothing in it.
abstract.cn: 手握紧了，里面却空着。

abstract.en: A page read five times without a single word staying.
abstract.cn: 一页看了五遍，一个字也没留下。

examples.en: Try not to worry about the results.
examples.cn: 尽量别为结果担心。

examples.en: His silence worried everyone at the table.
examples.cn: 他的沉默让桌边所有人都担心起来。

examples.en: Her main worry was how to pay the rent.
examples.cn: 她最大的烦恼是怎么付房租。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我瑞」——心里总觉着不祥的「瑞」兆要出事，于是担心。

root: 古英语 wyrgan（勒死、扼住），中古英语转为「咬住甩动」，近代英语才引申为「心里反复咬住一件事」，即担心。

sensesIntro.en: The throat grip comes first, then the bite that shakes, then the anxious mind, then the anxiety passed to others, and finally the anxiety itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是扼喉，再是咬住甩动，接着是焦灼的心，然后是把焦虑传给别人，最后是焦虑本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thought circling deeper hour after hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个念头越绕越紧。

branches.en: The anxiety branch: a letter that will surely arrive.
branches.cn: 焦虑分支：信总会到的。

branches.en: The causing branch: silence that makes others uneasy.
branches.cn: 致忧分支：让旁人不安的沉默。

branches.en: The noun branch: rent as the biggest worry.
branches.cn: 名词分支：最大的烦恼是房租。

branches.en: The bite branch: a dog shaking an old shoe.
branches.cn: 咬分支：狗甩旧鞋。

branches.en: The everyday branch: the same word for the feeling and the cause.
branches.cn: 日常分支：感受与来源共用一词。

intro.en: Worry is a bare stem whose y changes to i before endings, and -ing and -ed build its adjectives.
intro.cn: worry 是裸词干，加词尾时 y 变 i，-ing 与 -ed 构成它的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin words below name a close feeling from another tradition.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语；下面的拉丁词从另一传统来指相近的感受。

items.exampleCN: 它解释了 worried 的写法。

definition_zh: 崇拜；敬仰；礼拜；做礼拜
definition_en: to show deep respect and love for a god, or to admire someone greatly; also the act or service of such respect
core_image: 一个人弯下腰去，额头几乎触到地面
scene: 老庙的门槛被几代人的膝盖磨得凹下去一块。Every morning the villagers come to worship at the small shrine by the river.
sceneCN: 这里 worship 是「崇拜、敬拜」（第 1 个义项：对神或极受敬重者表达深深的敬意）；句意为每天早晨村民们都到河边那座小庙里敬拜。弯腰到额头几乎触地的姿态，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 worship 加 -er 构成，义为「崇拜者；礼拜者」
由 worship 加 -ful 构成，义为「恭敬的；崇拜的」
由 worshipful 加 -ly 构成，义为「恭敬地」

senses.title: Reverence for a god
senses.definition: to give a god the highest honour with prayer and ritual
senses.definitionCN: 以祈祷与仪式给神灵最高的敬意
senses.example: Every morning the villagers come to worship at the small shrine by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 每天早晨村民们到河边那座小庙里敬拜。
senses.why: The compound said worth-ship, the state of being worthy, and its highest form was honour paid to a god.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词原说 worth-ship（有价值、配得尊敬的状态），其最高形式就是对神的敬意。

senses.title: Deep admiration for a person
senses.definition: to admire someone so much that one almost overlooks their faults
senses.definitionCN: 极其钦佩某人，几乎看不到其缺点
senses.example: The young players worship the old coach who trained them.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻球员们非常崇拜训练他们的老教练。
senses.why: Because the word names deserved honour rather than only divine honour, it fits a person who has earned respect.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指应得的敬意而不只是对神的敬意，所以也能用于赢得尊重的人。

senses.title: The service itself
senses.definition: the religious ceremony at which such honour is given
senses.definitionCN: 举行这种敬意仪式的宗教活动
senses.example: The church holds worship at ten on Sunday mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 这所教堂周日上午十点举行礼拜。
senses.why: The state of honouring turns into the gathering where it happens, so the noun names an event.
senses.whyCN: 敬奉的状态变成了举行敬奉的聚会，于是名词也指一场活动。

senses.title: To be treated with such honour
senses.definition: to be the one before whom others bow, said of a place or an image
senses.definitionCN: 被人俯身敬奉的对象，就地点或圣像而言
senses.example: The old stone figure was worshipped long before the village had a name.
senses.exampleCN: 那座古老石像受敬奉的年代，远比村子有名字要早。
senses.why: The verb turns round: the one who receives the bowing is now the subject of the passive form.
senses.whyCN: 动词转了向：接受敬拜的一方，成了被动形式的主语。

intro.en: Worship is Old English weorthscipe, worth-ship, the condition of being worthy of honour, and only later the honour paid to God.
intro.cn: worship 来自古英语 weorthscipe，即 worth-ship，意为「配得尊敬的状态」，后来才指对神的敬奉。

items.en: weorthscipe joined weorth, worth, with scipe, a state or condition.
items.cn: weorthscipe 由 weorth（值得）与 scipe（状态）复合。

items.en: In early use it named the honour that a worthy person deserved.
items.cn: 早期用法指可敬之人应得的尊敬。

items.en: The spelling shortened to worship, and the suffix -ship kept its meaning.
items.cn: 拼写缩短为 worship，后缀 -ship 保留原意。

items.en: Religious use became dominant, so the word now means honour given to a god.
items.cn: 宗教用法占据主导，如今这个词指对神的敬意。

items.en: A title, as in Your Worship, still carries the old sense of deserved honour.
items.cn: 「Your Worship」这样的称呼仍带着「应得的尊敬」这一旧义。

note.en: The first group holds the word's own forms, the second holds other words for honour and religious service.
note.cn: 第一组收这个词自己的形式，第二组收其他表示敬意与宗教仪式的词。

entries.definition: A person who worships.
Full of respect, now formal.
Third person singular.
To love or respect deeply.
To respect with something like awe.
To speak to a god in words.

normalIntro.en: Worship is worth plus ship, the suffix that names a condition, as in friendship.
normalIntro.cn: worship 是 worth 加 ship，这个后缀表示状态，如 friendship。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the p before a vowel ending: worshipped.
normal.cn: 英式拼写在元音词尾前双写 p：worshipped。

normal.en: Worship is the noun and the verb at once, so only position tells them apart.
normal.cn: worship 同时是名词和动词，只靠位置区分。

normal.en: The suffix -ship is the same one in friendship and hardship.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ship 与 friendship、hardship 里的是同一个。

normal.en: Keep the r in the middle: worship is not warship, a naval vessel.
normal.cn: 中间保留 r：worship 不是 warship（军舰）。

normal.en: A place of worship is simply a building where people pray.
normal.cn: a place of worship 就是人们祈祷的建筑。

abstract.en: A threshold worn into a hollow by generations of knees.
abstract.cn: 门槛被几代人跪出凹陷。

abstract.en: A body bending until the forehead nearly touches stone.
abstract.cn: 身体弯下去，额头几乎触到石头。

abstract.en: A name said softly, as if it might break.
abstract.cn: 一个说得很轻的名字，仿佛一用力就会碎。

examples.en: People of many faiths worship in that old building.
examples.cn: 许多信仰的人都在那座老建筑里礼拜。

examples.en: Children often worship a teacher who treats them fairly.
examples.cn: 孩子常常特别崇敬公正对待他们的老师。

examples.en: The temple has been a place of worship for six hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座寺庙作为礼拜场所已有六百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我惜」——心里珍重到「我惜」二字的程度，就是崇拜。

root: 古英语 weorthscipe = weorth（值得、可贵）+ scipe（状态），原义「配得尊敬的状态」，后专指对神的敬奉。

sensesIntro.en: Deserved honour comes first, then the honour given to a god, then to a person, then the ceremony, and finally the one so honoured.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是应得的尊敬，再是对神的敬奉，接着是对人的崇敬，然后是仪式本身，最后是被敬奉者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body bending until the forehead nearly touches stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：弯到额头几乎触地的身体。

branches.en: The god branch: villagers at a riverside shrine.
branches.cn: 神灵分支：河边小庙里的村民。

branches.en: The person branch: players admiring an old coach.
branches.cn: 人分支：球员崇敬老教练。

branches.en: The service branch: ten o'clock worship on Sunday.
branches.cn: 仪式分支：周日十点的礼拜。

branches.en: The image branch: a stone figure honoured before the village had a name.
branches.cn: 圣像分支：村子未得名时已受敬奉的石像。

branches.en: The degree branch: the same word for a god and for a teacher.
branches.cn: 程度分支：对神与对老师用同一个词。

intro.en: Worship was built from two native parts, worth and -ship, and it still carries the colour of deserving.
intro.cn: worship 由两个本土成分构成：worth 与 -ship，至今仍带着「配得上」的意味。

latinIntro.en: Neither part is Latin; the Latin words below name devotion from another tradition.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都不是拉丁语；下面的拉丁词从另一传统来指虔敬。

items.example: It says what makes a person honoured.
It forms worship, as in friendship.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 worship，如 friendship 里的 -ship。

items.example: It shares the same letters at the start.
Warship is the one with an a.

definition_zh: 价值；值……钱；值得；有用；财产
definition_en: the value of something in money or in importance, or deserving of something
core_image: 秤盘上放一件旧东西，指针停在一个谁都说不上来的刻度
scene: 旧货摊上，摊主看了看那只表，摇了摇头说这表不值几个钱，但时间准得让人舍不得扔。The old bicycle is not worth much, but I would not sell it for anything.
sceneCN: 这里 worth 是「价值、值（多少钱）」（第 1 个义项：事物在金钱或重要性上可衡量的价值）；句意为这辆旧自行车不值多少钱，但我多少钱也不卖。秤盘上那件东西停在一个不好说的刻度上，就是这个词的印象。

collocations.zh: 不管有没有用；仅供参考

derivatives.zh: 由 worth 加 -y 构成，义为「值得的；可敬的」
由 worth 加 -less 构成，义为「无价值的；没用的」
由 worth 与 while 复合，义为「值得花时间的」
由 worthy 加 -ness 构成，义为「值得；可贵」

senses.title: Value in money
senses.definition: the amount of money that something would bring if sold
senses.definitionCN: 某物出售时能得到的钱数
senses.example: The old bicycle is not worth much, but I would not sell it for anything.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧自行车不值多少钱，但我多少钱也不卖。
senses.why: The core meaning is measured value: how much a thing is worth on a scale of money.
senses.whyCN: 核心意思是可衡量的价值：一件东西在钱的刻度上值多少。

senses.title: Deserving of something
senses.definition: having enough value or merit to justify the cost, effort or time
senses.definitionCN: 有价值到足以抵得上所付出的钱、力或时间
senses.example: This book is worth reading twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书值得读两遍。
senses.why: Once value is measured against effort, the word turns into a judgement: is the cost repaid?
senses.whyCN: 一旦把价值与付出相比，这个词就变成一种判断：所付是否值得。

senses.title: The quality that matters
senses.definition: the real importance or usefulness of a person or thing, apart from money
senses.definitionCN: 人或物在金钱之外的真实重要性或用处
senses.example: He proved his worth in the first month of the job.
senses.exampleCN: 他在工作的第一个月就证明了自己的价值。
senses.why: Once the scale is not money but usefulness, the same noun measures a person instead of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 当刻度不是钱而是用处时，同一个名词衡量的就从物变成了人。

senses.title: What one owns
senses.definition: the total of a person's money and property, as in net worth
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的钱财与产业总额，如 net worth
senses.example: The fire took everything of worth in the house.
senses.exampleCN: 那场火烧掉了屋里所有值钱的东西。
senses.why: The noun can also gather all the valuable things together, so it names a body of property.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也能把值钱的东西收拢在一起，于是指一整套财产。

intro.en: Worth is Old English weorth, meaning value or price, related to the verb weorthan, to become.
intro.cn: worth 来自古英语 weorth，意为价值或价格，与动词 weorthan（成为）相关。

items.en: weorth named the value of a thing, what it was reckoned at.
items.cn: weorth 指一物的价值，即它被估作多少。

items.en: Cousin words in German and Dutch still mean worth or value.
items.cn: 德语与荷兰语的同源词仍表示价值。

items.en: worth was used with a following noun of price, as worth ten pounds.
items.cn: worth 后面常接表示价钱的名词，如 worth ten pounds。

items.en: The adjective use without a verb grew fixed, as in worth a try.
items.cn: 不带系动词的形容词用法固定下来，如 worth a try。

items.en: The suffix -ship built worship from it, and -y built worthy.
items.cn: 后缀 -ship 由它造出 worship，-y 造出 worthy。

note.en: The first group holds the derivatives that grow from this root, the second holds other words for value.
note.cn: 第一组收由这个词根长出的派生词，第二组收其他表示价值的词。

entries.definition: Deserving respect or attention.
Having no value at all.
Worth the time spent on it.
The amount of money a thing is worth.
The money asked for a thing.
The quality of deserving praise.

normalIntro.en: Worth is an uninflected adjective and a noun at the same time, and the th is soft.
normalIntro.cn: worth 同时是不变化的形容词和名词，th 发清音。

normal.en: Worth is followed by a noun or an -ing word, never by to: worth reading, not worth to read.
normal.cn: worth 后接名词或 -ing 形式，不用 to：worth reading，而非 worth to read。

normal.en: The th is the unvoiced one, as in think, not the one in this.
normal.cn: 这里的 th 是清音，如 think，而不是 this 里的浊音。

normal.en: Worthless and worthy are opposites built with two different endings.
normal.cn: worthless 与 worthy 是用两种词尾造出的一对反义词。

normal.en: Worthwhile joins worth and while, since time is what is spent.
normal.cn: worthwhile 由 worth 与 while 复合，因为花掉的是时间。

normal.en: Worship was once worth-ship, which links honour with value.
normal.cn: worship 原是 worth-ship，把敬意与价值连在一起。

abstract.en: A pointer stopped at a mark nobody can quite read.
abstract.cn: 指针停在一个谁也读不准的刻度上。

abstract.en: A watch kept for its accuracy rather than its price.
abstract.cn: 一只留着是因为准，而不是因为值钱。

abstract.en: A month of work that answers a question about a person.
abstract.cn: 一个月的工作回答了一个关于人的问题。

examples.en: The tickets are worth every penny.
examples.cn: 这些票每一分钱都值。

examples.en: It is worth asking him before you decide.
examples.cn: 决定之前值得问问他。

examples.en: She proved her worth as a member of the team.
examples.cn: 她证明了自己作为队员的价值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我思」——值得的东西，值得「我思」上一整天。

root: 古英语 weorth（价值；价格），与 weorthan（成为）相关；-y 得 worthy，-less 得 worthless，-ship 得 worship。

sensesIntro.en: Measured value comes first, then the judgement that a cost is repaid, then the importance that money cannot measure, and finally the property one owns.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是可衡量的价值，再是「付出的值得」这一判断，接着是钱量不出的重要性，最后是拥有的财产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pointer stopped at an unreadable mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：停在读不准的刻度上的指针。

branches.en: The price branch: a bicycle worth very little.
branches.cn: 价钱分支：不值多少钱的自行车。

branches.en: The judgement branch: a book worth reading twice.
branches.cn: 判断分支：值得读两遍的书。

branches.en: The person branch: proving worth in a first month.
branches.cn: 人分支：第一个月就证明价值。

branches.en: The property branch: everything of worth lost in a fire.
branches.cn: 财产分支：火中失去的所有值钱之物。

branches.en: The measure branch: one word for price and for human worth.
branches.cn: 衡量分支：一个词兼指价钱与人的价值。

intro.en: Worth is a bare stem, and three endings give it three very different children: worthy, worthless and worship.
intro.cn: worth 是裸词干，三个词尾生出三个很不一样的孩子：worthy、worthless 与 worship。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin words below measure value and merit in another tradition.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语；下面的拉丁词在另一传统中衡量价值与功劳。

definition_zh: 值得的；配得上的；可敬的；有价值的
definition_en: deserving something good, or having enough merit to be respected
core_image: 一件旧外套洗得发白、补过两次，但穿它的人站得很直
scene: 评选名单上，那个默默做了十年杂事的人排在最前面。Her work with the children is worthy of more attention than it gets.
sceneCN: 这里 worthy 是「值得的、配得上的」（第 1 个义项：理应得到某种好的对待）；句意为她为孩子们所做的工作理应得到更多关注，而实际得到的太少。洗得发白却站得笔直的旧外套，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 要人；知名人士（多带调侃）

derivatives.zh: 由 worthy 加 -ness 构成，义为「值得；可贵之处」
由 worthy 加 -ly 构成，义为「值得地；相称地」
由 worthy 加前缀 un- 构成，义为「不值得的；不相称的」
由 praise 与 worthy 复合，义为「值得称赞的」

senses.title: Deserving of something
senses.definition: having enough value to deserve a particular good thing, as in worthy of praise
senses.definitionCN: 有价值到理应得到某种好的对待，如 worthy of praise
senses.example: Her work with the children is worthy of more attention than it gets.
senses.exampleCN: 她为孩子们所做的工作理应得到更多关注，而实际得到的太少。
senses.why: The root is worth, so the adjective says a person or thing has enough value to deserve its reward.
senses.whyCN: 词根是 worth，所以这个形容词表示某人某物有足够价值，理应得到那份回报。

senses.title: Respectable in itself
senses.definition: having the qualities that earned respect, often used of effort and character
senses.definitionCN: 具备赢来尊敬的那些品质，常用于努力与品性
senses.example: It is a worthy attempt even if it did not succeed.
senses.exampleCN: 即使没有成功，这也是一次可敬的尝试。
senses.why: The frame worthy of can drop its object, leaving the sense that the effort itself carries merit.
senses.whyCN: worthy of 的句式可以省去对象，留下「这份努力本身就有价值」的意思。

senses.title: The local notable
senses.definition: used as a noun, often with a touch of mockery, for a local person of standing
senses.definitionCN: 作名词用，常带一点调侃，指地方上有地位的人
senses.example: The town worthies gathered on the platform to give short speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的头面人物都聚到台上做简短的讲话。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for people who are thought to embody worth, and the tone turns dry.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指被认为有分量的人，语气随之带上了干涩的调侃。

senses.title: Worth the trouble
senses.definition: used of a cause or a thing that justifies the effort put into it
senses.definitionCN: 用于值得为之付出的事业或事物
senses.example: The repair of the old bridge is a worthy cause for the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 重修这座老桥是对整个村子都值得的一件事。
senses.why: Applied to a cause, the word answers the question whether the effort will be repaid.
senses.whyCN: 用到一件事上时，这个词回答的是「这份力气会不会有回报」。

intro.en: Worthy is Old English weorthig, worth plus the adjective ending -ig, then -y in modern spelling.
intro.cn: worthy 来自古英语 weorthig，即 worth 加形容词词尾 -ig，现代拼写变为 -y。

items.en: The adjective weorthig said that a thing had worth and so deserved regard.
items.cn: 形容词 weorthig 表示某物有价值，因而值得看重。

items.en: The ending weakened, giving worthy, and the noun use appeared.
items.cn: 词尾弱化，形成 worthy，名词用法也随之出现。

items.en: Worthy of became the standard frame for saying what is deserved.
items.cn: worthy of 成了表示「配得上」的标准句式。

items.en: In speech the adjective can sound a little stiff, which is why self-made uses poke fun.
items.cn: 口语中这个形容词略显板正，所以有些用法是拿来打趣的。

items.en: Unworthy and praiseworthy show how freely the word compounds.
items.cn: unworthy 与 praiseworthy 说明这个词复合得多么自由。

note.en: The first group holds the family around worth, the second holds adjectives of deserving and of respect.
note.cn: 第一组收 worth 周围的家族词，第二组收表示值得与可敬的形容词。

entries.definition: Value, or deserving of something.
The quality of deserving respect.
Not deserving, or not good enough.
Having earned good treatment.
Deserving respect and approval.
Of a good social standing, decent.

normalIntro.en: Worthy is worth plus y, with the comparison taking -ier and -iest.
normalIntro.cn: worthy 是 worth 加 -y，比较级和最高级分别用 -ier 与 -iest。

normal.en: The y turns to i in the comparison: worthier and worthiest.
normal.cn: 比较级里 y 变 i：worthier 与 worthiest。

normal.en: Worthy of is the frame: worthy of praise, worthy of note.
normal.cn: 常用框架是 worthy of：worthy of praise、worthy of note。

normal.en: Add un- for the opposite: unworthy of the honour.
normal.cn: 加 un- 得反义：unworthy of the honour。

normal.en: The ringing is voiced here, unlike the th in worth, because the ending is voiced too.
normal.cn: 这里的 th 发浊音，与 worth 的清音不同，因为词尾也是浊音。

normal.en: Praiseworthy and noteworthy are compounds, and both keep the y.
normal.cn: praiseworthy 与 noteworthy 都是复合词，都保留 y。

abstract.en: A coat washed pale and mended twice, worn by someone standing straight.
abstract.cn: 洗得发白、补过两次的外套，穿着它的人站得很直。

abstract.en: A name on a list placed above louder names.
abstract.cn: 名单上的一个名字排在更响的名字之上。

abstract.en: A hand held out to an opponent who fought well.
abstract.cn: 伸手递给一个打得好的对手。

examples.en: The plan is worthy of serious discussion.
examples.cn: 这个方案值得认真讨论。

examples.en: He is a worthy opponent and a fair player.
examples.cn: 他是个值得尊敬的对手，也打得公道。

examples.en: Teaching the children to read is a worthy cause.
examples.cn: 教孩子们读书是一件值得做的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我值」——我「值」得这份尊敬，就是 worthy。

root: 古英语 weorthig = weorth（价值）+ -ig（形容词词尾，今作 -y）；比较级 worthier，反义 unworthy。

sensesIntro.en: Deserving a reward comes first, then being respectable in oneself, then the humorous use as a noun, and finally the cause worth doing for.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是理应得到回报，再是自身可敬，然后是带调侃的名词用法，最后是值得去做的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mended coat worn by someone standing straight.
core.cn: 核心意象：补过的旧外套，穿着的人站得笔直。

branches.en: The deserving branch: work worthy of more attention.
branches.cn: 应得分支：理应得到更多关注的工作。

branches.en: The character branch: a worthy attempt that failed.
branches.cn: 品性分支：失败却可敬的尝试。

branches.en: The noun branch: town worthies giving speeches.
branches.cn: 名词分支：镇上头面人物讲话。

branches.en: The cause branch: repairing the old bridge.
branches.cn: 事业分支：重修老桥。

branches.en: The frame branch: worthy of plus a noun is the usual shape.
branches.cn: 句式分支：常用 worthy of 接名词。

intro.en: Worthy is a stem plus -y, and it still lives by the frame worthy of.
intro.cn: worthy 是词干加 -y，至今仍活在 worthy of 这个句式里。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin words below express deserving with a different verb.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语；下面的拉丁词用另一个动词表达「值得」。

definition_zh: 伤口；创伤；伤害；使受伤；伤害（感情）
definition_en: an injury that breaks the skin or cuts deeply, or to cause such an injury; also to hurt someone's feelings
core_image: 小臂上一道已经结痂的口子，边缘还红着一圈
scene: 包扎完以后，大夫叮嘱这两天别沾水，也别去搬重东西。The wound on his arm healed quickly, but he still avoided lifting heavy boxes.
sceneCN: 这里 wound 是「伤口」（第 1 个义项：使皮肤破损或深深切开的损伤）；句意为他手臂上的伤口好得很快，但他仍不愿搬重箱子。手臂上那圈还红着的口子，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wound 加 -ed 构成，义为「受伤的」
由 wound 加 -ing 构成，义为「伤人的；刺痛的」
由 wound 加 -less 构成，义为「未受伤的」

senses.title: The physical injury
senses.definition: an injury in which the skin is cut or broken, especially by a weapon
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤被切开或打破的损伤，尤指由武器造成
senses.example: The wound on his arm healed quickly, but he still avoided lifting heavy boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 他手臂上的伤口好得很快，但他仍不愿搬重箱子。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a blow that breaks the surface of the body, and that body image runs through the others.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是打破身体表面的击伤，这个身体形象贯穿其余义项。

senses.title: To injure
senses.definition: to hurt a person or animal so that the skin or flesh is broken
senses.definitionCN: 使皮肤或皮肉破损地伤害人或动物
senses.example: Two men were wounded in the accident at the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 路口那场事故中有两人受伤。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb that names the act which produces it, and the passive is the common shape.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词，指造成这个结果的动作，常用被动形式。

senses.title: The hurt that cannot be seen
senses.definition: to damage someone in feeling or reputation, not in the body
senses.definitionCN: 在情感或名誉上而非身体上伤害某人
senses.example: Her remark wounded him more than any accident could have.
senses.exampleCN: 她那句话对他的刺痛，胜过任何一场事故。
senses.why: The body image carries over: an unseen cut in feeling uses the same word as a cut in the skin.
senses.whyCN: 身体形象延续下来：看不见的情感切口，用与皮肤切口同一个词。

senses.title: The injury to a cause
senses.definition: a lasting damage done to a plan, a group or a reputation
senses.definitionCN: 对计划、团体或声誉造成的持久损害
senses.example: The decision was a wound to the trust between the two towns.
senses.exampleCN: 那个决定是两个镇之间的信任上的一道伤。
senses.why: When the thing hurt is a bond rather than a body, the word still marks while it leaves a lasting mark.
senses.whyCN: 当受伤的不是身体而是联系时，这个词照样留下持久的痕迹。

intro.en: Wound is Old English wund, a physical injury, shared with German Wunde, and unrelated to the past tense of wind.
intro.cn: wound 来自古英语 wund（身体损伤），与德语 Wunde 同源，与 wind 的过去式毫无关系。

items.en: wund meant a cut or a blow that breaks the body.
items.cn: wund 指切开或打破身体的伤。

items.en: The same noun appears in German and Dutch for the same kind of injury.
items.cn: 同一名词在德语与荷兰语里指同样的损伤。

items.en: The word was used for battle injuries and spread to the verb.
items.cn: 这个词用于战伤，并蔓延到动词用法。

items.en: The figurative sense of hurting feelings settled in ordinary use.
items.cn: 伤害感情的比喻义在日常用法中固定下来。

items.en: It is spelled like wound, the past of wind, and the two are pronounced alike but unrelated.
items.cn: 它拼得与 wind 的过去式 wound 一样，两者读音相同却毫无关系。

note.en: The first group holds the forms of this word, including the look-alike past of wind, the second holds other words for injury.
note.cn: 第一组收本词的各种形式，包括形同的 wind 过去式，第二组收其他表示损伤的词。

entries.definition: Hurt, in body or in feeling.
More than one wound, or third person singular.
Twisted or turned, the past of wind.
Physical harm to the body.
The mark left after a wound heals.
An opening made in the skin by something sharp.

normalIntro.en: Wound keeps the ou spelling but has a long oo sound, and it must not be confused with the past of wind.
normalIntro.cn: wound 保留了 ou 的拼写，却读长音，且不能与 wind 的过去式混淆。

normal.en: The spelling ou here is regular: wound rhymes with spoon, not with ground.
normal.cn: 这里的 ou 读长音：wound 与 spoon 押韵，不与 ground 押韵。

normal.en: Wound as the past of wind is pronounced differently and means twisted.
normal.cn: 作 wind 的过去式时读音不同，意思是缠绕。

normal.en: Wounded is the usual adjective: a wounded soldier.
normal.cn: 常用形容词是 wounded：a wounded soldier。

normal.en: The verb has three senses: hurt the body, hurt the feelings, hurt a cause.
normal.cn: 这个动词有三义：伤身体、伤感情、伤事业。

normal.en: Lick one's wounds means to rest and recover after a defeat.
normal.cn: lick one's wounds 指受挫后休整恢复。

abstract.en: A line of scab with a red rim still around it.
abstract.cn: 一道结痂的口子，边上一圈还红着。

abstract.en: A bandage still on a forearm two days later.
abstract.cn: 两天后小臂上还缠着绷带。

abstract.en: A sentence that stays with a person far longer than any cut.
abstract.cn: 一句话在人心里留得比任何伤口都久。

examples.en: The wound was small but deep, and it took weeks to close.
examples.cn: 伤口不大却很深，好几周才合上。

examples.en: He was wounded in the shoulder during the match.
examples.cn: 比赛时他肩膀受了伤。

examples.en: Her words had wounded him, even if she meant no harm.
examples.cn: 她的话伤了他，尽管她并无恶意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捂」——伤口不能碰，只好捂着。

root: 古英语 wund（身体创伤），与德语 Wunde 同源；与 wind 的过去式 wound 仅为同形，无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: The broken skin comes first, then the act of breaking it, then the doing of it to feelings, and finally to a cause or a bond.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是破开的皮肤，再是打破它的动作，接着是对感情下手，最后到事业或关系上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scab with a red rim around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：结痂却还红着的口子。

branches.en: The injury branch: a wound slow to close.
branches.cn: 伤口分支：迟迟不合的口子。

branches.en: The harm branch: wounded in the shoulder during a match.
branches.cn: 伤害分支：比赛中肩膀受伤。

branches.en: The feeling branch: words that hurt more than accidents.
branches.cn: 情感分支：比事故更刺痛的话。

branches.en: The lasting branch: trust between two towns damaged.
branches.cn: 持久分支：两镇之间受损的信任。

branches.en: The image branch: the body wound gives the feeling the same word.
branches.cn: 形象分支：身体之伤把同一个词给了情感。

intro.en: Wound is a bare stem; -ed and -ing build its forms, and the spelling also belongs to another verb entirely.
intro.cn: wound 是裸词干；-ed 与 -ing 构成其余形式，而这个拼写还属于另一个动词。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin words below name injury and its mark.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语；下面的拉丁词指损伤及其痕迹。

items.example: Its past tense is also wound.
It sounds like the oo in spoon.
items.exampleCN: 读起来像 spoon 里的 oo。

definition_zh: 包；裹；缠绕；围住；（使）结束；（电影）拍完
definition_en: to cover something by folding paper or cloth around it, or to wind something around; also to finish an activity
core_image: 把东西放进去，四角折过来，一条细绳绕三圈系住
scene: 生日前夜，桌上摆着剪好的纸和一卷彩色带子，礼物还露着一角。She wrapped the bowl in newspaper so it would survive the journey.
sceneCN: 这里 wrap 是「包、裹」（第 1 个义项：用纸或布把东西折起来盖住）；句意为她用报纸把碗包好，好让它经得住颠簸。四角折过来、细绳绕三圈，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wrap 加 -er 构成，义为「包装纸；封套」
由 wrap 加 -ing 构成，义为「包装材料」
由 wrap 加 -ed 构成，义为「包好的；入神的」

senses.title: To cover it round
senses.definition: to fold paper or cloth right round a thing so that it is covered on all sides
senses.definitionCN: 把纸或布整个折起来围住某物，使其四面都被盖住
senses.example: She wrapped the bowl in newspaper so it would survive the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 她用报纸把碗包好，好让它经得住颠簸。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to wind cloth around something, and every other sense is that motion again.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是把布绕在东西上，其余义项都是这个动作的再现。

senses.title: To wind round and round
senses.definition: to put something such as a band or a cord round a thing several times
senses.definitionCN: 把带子、绳子之类在物体上绕好几圈
senses.example: A thin ribbon was wrapped twice around the box.
senses.exampleCN: 一条细带子在盒子上绕了两圈。
senses.why: The same motion is now used with a cord instead of a sheet, so the word still means to circle a thing.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作换成绳而不是布，这个词仍然是把东西绕起来。

senses.title: To finish something
senses.definition: to bring an activity, a meeting or a filming to its end, as in wrap up
senses.definitionCN: 让一项活动、会议或拍摄告一段落，如 wrap up
senses.example: Let us wrap up the meeting before the train leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 咱们趁火车开走之前把会开完。
senses.why: When work is wrapped up, the last loose ends are folded in as if they were being covered, and then the whole is closed.
senses.whyCN: 把工作「包完」，就是把最后几处散头折进去，像盖住一样，然后把整体合上。

senses.title: To be absorbed in something
senses.definition: to give all one's attention to something, as in wrapped up in
senses.definitionCN: 把全部注意力放在某事上，如 wrapped up in
senses.example: He was so wrapped up in his book that he missed his stop.
senses.exampleCN: 他看得太入神，坐过了站。
senses.why: Attention wound tightly around one subject leaves nothing outside, so a person inside a book is wrapped in it.
senses.whyCN: 注意力紧紧绕在一个主题上，外面就什么都不剩，于是埋头读书的人便是被书「裹住」了。

intro.en: Wrap is of uncertain origin, appearing in Middle English as wrappen, and probably related to the older sense of turning and rolling.
intro.cn: wrap 的词源不确定，中古英语作 wrappen，可能与其更早的「翻转、滚卷」之意相关。

items.en: wrappen meant to wind or to fold a covering round something.
items.cn: wrappen 意为缠绕或用覆布把某物包起来。

items.en: No older Germanic form is certainly related, and its ancestry is still argued.
items.cn: 没有确定的更早日耳曼语形式与之相关，其渊源至今仍有争议。

items.en: The ending -er built wrapper for the paper and the cover.
items.cn: 后缀 -er 造出 wrapper，指包装纸与封套。

items.en: The sense to finish grew in American film making, where a shot was wrapped.
items.cn: 「结束」这一义项在美国电影制作中生长出来，镜头拍完就叫 wrapped。

items.en: The phrase under wraps, kept secret, comes from cloth keeping a thing hidden.
items.cn: under wraps（保密）来自用布把东西盖住藏起来。

note.en: The first group holds the derived forms, the second holds other verbs for covering and binding.
note.cn: 第一组收派生形式，第二组收其他表示包裹与捆扎的动词。

entries.definition: Covered, or wholly absorbed in something.
The paper or cover around a thing.
Material used for wrapping.
To put something over a thing.
To tie or fasten together.
To bend something over on itself.

normalIntro.en: Wrap ends in a single p, but doubles it before a vowel ending: wrapped, wrapping.
normalIntro.cn: wrap 末尾只有一个 p，但在元音词尾前要双写：wrapped、wrapping。

normal.en: Double the p before -ed and -ing: wrapped and wrapping, not wraped.
normal.cn: -ed 与 -ing 前双写 p：wrapped、wrapping，而不是 wraped。

normal.en: The past tense is wrapped, not wraped, because wrap is a one-syllable word ending in p.
normal.cn: 过去式是 wrapped，因为 wrap 是单音节且以 p 结尾。

normal.en: Wrap up means both to cover and to finish, so context decides.
normal.cn: wrap up 既指包起来也指结束，看上下文定。

normal.en: Under wraps means hidden from everyone, like a gift before the day.
normal.cn: under wraps 指藏起来不让知道，如节前的礼物。

normal.en: Rap is the look-alike with one p, meaning to knock; wrap with w covers.
normal.cn: 单写 p 的 rap 是敲击；带 w 的 wrap 是包裹。

abstract.en: Four corners folded in, then a string wound three times.
abstract.cn: 四角折进来，再绕三圈绳。

abstract.en: A gift still showing one corner of paper.
abstract.cn: 礼物还露着一角纸。

abstract.en: A person so inside a book that the world outside stops.
abstract.cn: 一个人陷在书里，外面的世界停了。

examples.en: Please wrap the glasses in paper before packing them.
examples.cn: 装之前请把杯子用纸包一下。

examples.en: We should wrap up the report before Friday.
examples.cn: 我们应该在周五之前把报告收尾。

examples.en: The present is still under wraps until his birthday.
examples.cn: 礼物到他生日之前一直保密。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「绕」——把东西一绕一包，就是 wrap。

root: 中古英语 wrappen（缠绕、包覆），更早来源不确定；加 -ed、-ing 时双写 p；-er 构成 wrapper。

sensesIntro.en: The cloth goes round the thing, then the cord winds round it, then the session is wound up, and finally attention is wound around one subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是布绕上东西，再是绳绕上东西，接着是把一场活动绕完，最后是把注意力绕在一件事上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four corners folded in, a string wound three times.
core.cn: 核心意象：四角折入，绳绕三圈。

branches.en: The covering branch: a bowl wrapped in newspaper.
branches.cn: 包裹分支：用报纸包起的碗。

branches.en: The winding branch: ribbon wrapped twice around a box.
branches.cn: 缠绕分支：绕了两圈的带子。

branches.en: The ending branch: wrapping up a meeting before a train.
branches.cn: 结束分支：赶火车前把会开完。

branches.en: The absorption branch: too deep in a book to notice the stop.
branches.cn: 专注分支：看书入神坐过站。

branches.en: The privacy branch: kept under wraps, like a covered gift.
branches.cn: 隐秘分支：像盖住的礼物一样保密。

intro.en: Wrap is a short stem with a doubled p before endings, and -er and -ing build its nouns.
intro.cn: wrap 是短词干，词尾前双写 p，-er 与 -ing 构成其名词。

latinIntro.en: The stem has no Latin ancestor; the words below cover the same action from the Latin side.
latinIntro.cn: 词干没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词从拉丁语一侧表达同样的动作。
